number, policy type, and policy start date. Code the content using GTL, SSJS, or AMPscript to use the

JSON formatted content in the data extension.

8. 8.  Click Preview and Test and select the data extension from Data 360.

Create a Welcome Series in Journey Builder

Now that the emails are complete, you can create the journey.

1. 1.  In Marketing Cloud Engagement, go to Journey Builder.

2. 2.  Click Create New Journey.

3. 3.  Select Multi-Step Journey and then click Create.

4. 4.  For the entry source, drag a Data Extension activity to the canvas.

5. 5.  To select the New Auto Policy data extension, click the data extension activity.

6. 6.  Click Summary and then click Done.

7. 7.  Next drag an Email activity to the interface.

8. 8.  Click the email activity and then select the Cumulus Welcome - Tips for Getting Started Email after

clicking Select Message.

9. 9.  Click Summary to review Message Configuration, Delivery Options, and Advanced Options. Click

Done.

10. 10.  Repeat these steps for the other welcome emails.

11. 11.  Adjust the wait times between the emails to 3 days, 5 days, and 1 day.

12. 12.  To make this journey an ongoing campaign, click Schedule, Recurring, and then Select.

a. a.  Select a Start Date, Start Time, and Time Zone. For this campaign, select Weekly, on Monday, and

ending Never.

13. 13.  Click Contact Evaluation and select Evaluate new records only.

a. a.  For the first run, select to evaluate All records in the file.

14. 14.  Click Summary and then Done.

15. 15.  Review the journey and click Save.

16. 16.  To ensure that all information has been completed, click Validate.

17. 17.  Test the journey, and then click Activate when ready.

The campaign is ready for customers.

Data 360

Before you start using Data 360, review the checklist, considerations, and product navigation.

Note As of October 14, 2025, Data Cloud has been rebranded to Data 360. During this transition,

you may see references to Data Cloud in our application and documentation. While the name is

new, the functionality and content remains unchanged.

To get ready for Data 360, confirm your team:

•  Understands overall guidelines and limitations that can impact billing.
•  Reviews brand management and organization structure used in Data 360.
•  Decides on a data strategy by reviewing data model concepts.
•  Analyzes your existing data and data sources.
•  Plans to use unified profiles.
•  Identifies users and their needed permissions.
•  Identifies goals and determine how they want to use the data.

Checklist and Considerations

Download the interactive PDF worksheet: Data 360 Checklist and Considerations.

Navigation

Once Data 360 is enabled in your account, you can find Data Cloud in the App Launcher.

171

Data 360

Data 360 Cross-Product Solutions

On the Data Cloud home page, features are organized into tabs.

The Data Streams, Data Lake Objects, and Data Model (1) tabs are focused on data ingestion and

modeling.

Data Explorer and Profile Explorer (2) are data-viewing tools, allowing a view into ingested data and

unified profiles.

The Identity Resolutions (3) tab is where your team creates match and reconciliation rules to unify

individual records.

Calculated Insights (4) are predefined and calculated metrics that can be used in creating segments and

for data analysis.

The Setup gear (5) is where system admin and users with the Data 360 Architect permission set

configure Data 360 features.

Data 360 Licenses, Billing, and Limits

How you pay for data services provided by Data 360 depends on how your Data 360 org is licensed.

Your licenses determine both billing method and limits for your org. We recommend working with

your account exec before buying Data 360 or when your contract renews to ensure your license is the

best choice based on your usage and growth potential.

Data 360 Lifecycle Management

To manage your Data 360 lifecycle you can renew your license or delete your Data 360 instance to

set up a new Data 360 instance with an active license, use the Data 360 cleanup process to delete its

associated data, metadata, and configurations. You can also use the cleanup process to connect your

org as a Data Cloud One companion to an existing Data 360 instance.

Einstein and Data Usage in Data 360

Einstein is built on data. When using Data 360, review this table to understand the type of data that

Data 360

Data 360 Licenses, Billing, and Limits

Data 360 Licenses, Billing, and Limits

How you pay for data services provided by Data 360 depends on how your Data 360 org is licensed. Your

licenses determine both billing method and limits for your org. We recommend working with your

account exec before buying Data 360 or when your contract renews to ensure your license is the best

choice based on your usage and growth potential.

All Data 360 licenses are add-ons to a Salesforce org license. Contact your account executive for a list of

Salesforce org licenses that Data 360 can be added onto.

All orgs in a Data 360 cluster, including the primary production Home org, sandbox orgs created from it,

its Data Cloud One Companion orgs, and their sandboxes, must all use the same type of Data 360

licenses. Data 360 license are managed by the production Home org, which is billed for data processing

workloads generated by its sandboxes and companion orgs.

Features powered by Data 360 including Agentforce and Agentforce Employee Agent, are billed for Data

360 services depending on the org’s Data 360 license type.

Data Cloud License

•  License: This license is available for purchase and renewal. A variety of add-ons can be used with this
license, including real-time profile processing and data governance features. See Data 360 Editions

and Licenses.

•  Billing: Orgs using the Data Cloud license are billed based on consumption of data storage and data
services in a variety of usage types. Depending on which credits your org purchases, credits are

decremented from either the Data Services or Flex Credits consumption card. See Data Services

Billable Usage Types for Data 360.

•  Limits: Data Cloud orgs must adhere to specific limits for some features. See Data 360 Limits and

Guidelines.

Data 360 Profiles License

•  License: This license is an add-on to the Data Cloud license. It changes billing and limits for some data

services. See Data 360 Profiles License Billing and Limits.

•  Billing: Orgs with this add-on license aren’t billed for batch data transforms, identity resolution

rulesets, segments, and batch calculated insights. Credits continue to be decremented from the Data

Services or Flex Credits card for all other types of usage. See Data 360 Profiles License Billing

Considerations.

•  Limits: Limits for data transforms, unified profiles, segments, and insights are determined by which
Data 360 Profile license you purchase. You can purchase higher limits for data transforms, segments,

and insights. However, the number of identity resolution rulesets you can create is determined by the

base Data 360 Profile license and can’t be increased. See Data 360 Profiles License Base License

Limits.

174

Data 360

Data 360 Licenses, Billing, and Limits

Customer Data Platform (CDP) License

•  License: This license is no longer available for purchase or renewal.
•  Billing: Orgs using the Customer Data Platform license are billed based on the number of profiles,

segment publishes, and engagement events their org completes. To understand billing calculations,

see Customer Data Platform Billable Usage Calculations.

•  Limits: Customer Data Platform orgs must adhere to specific limits for most features. Some Data 360
features aren’t available to orgs with this license type. To review limits, see Customer Data Platform

Limits and Guidelines.

Data 360 Editions and Licenses

Data 360 is available in several supported Salesforce editions. Some Data 360 features also require

additional licenses.

Data 360 Reportable Resource References

Resource references are standard usage tags that let you view your credit consumption by the feature
that generated the usage. You can build custom Data 360 reports on resource types to view, filter, and

sort your usage by its source.

Data Space References in Standard Consumption Tags

Filter and group reports about your Data 360 consumption usage by data space.

Reduce Credit Consumption in Data 360

You can reduce the number of credits consumed by Data 360 data services by updating settings on

features such as data streams, data transforms, identity resolution, and more. For most features,

reducing the amount of data processed or the frequency of processing reduces costs.

Billing Impact of Data 360–Powered Features

Some Salesforce CRM features are powered by Data 360 data. These features impact Data Services

Credit consumption by increasing usage of associated processes in Data 360 (such as querying,

storage, processing, and analytics). Before configuring Data 360-powered features, review feature and

usage documentation. Contact your account executive to understand how features impact Data

Services Credit consumption in Data 360.

Data Cloud License Billing and Limits

Adding a Data Cloud license enables Data 360 on a Salesforce org. Orgs with this license purchase

consumption credits which are consumed by use of Data 360 services.

Data 360 Profiles License Billing and Limits

Data 360 Profiles and Data 360 Enterprise Profiles licenses can be added on to Data Cloud licenses to

change how a Data 360 org is billed and limited. When a Data 360 org has this license, its identity

resolution rulesets, profiles, segments, data transforms, and insights are limited but don't consume

credits.

Customer Data Platform License Billing and Limits

Customers with this license have access to Data 360 on a Salesforce org. This license is no longer
available for purchase and can't be renewed. Orgs with this license are billed based on the numbers of

profiles, engagements, and other records in their orgs. Other features have limits. Not all Data 360

features are available on Data 360 orgs with this license.

Data 360 Reportable Resource References

Resource references are standard usage tags that let you view your credit consumption by the feature
that generated the usage. You can build custom Data 360 reports on resource types to view, filter, and
sort your usage by its source.

Note Resource references rolled out incrementally between July 2025 and September 2025. Data

178

Data 360

Data 360 Licenses, Billing, and Limits

isn’t available for a specific resource type prior to its rollout.

Because resource references are organized by feature, usage that is counted against different usage types

is sometimes bundled together. For example, batch connectors and streaming connectors consume

credits in different usage types, but are both reported by the same resource reference.

After creating a report on a Resource Type, sort by the Resource ID or API Name field to see what within

the feature generated usage. For example, if you create a report on the DataStreamDefinition resource

type, sorting by connector API names stored in the Resource ID or API Name field lets you see how

much each connection contributed to your usage.

Data Space References in Standard Consumption Tags

Filter and group reports about your Data 360 consumption usage by data space.

The data space name is captured in the Data Space API field in the TenantUsageAttrDetail data lake

object (DLO). To use it, build a Data 360 report that breaks down consumption by data space by joining

the TenantEnrichedUsageEvent and TenantUsageAttrDetail DLOs on Tenant Billing Usage Event Id.

You don’t consume credits when querying or reporting on these DLOs. You can build reports in other

ways, such as by reporting on the Consumption Insights Extended data model object (DMO) or creating

a Tableau Next Viz. Some reporting methods can consume credits.

Reduce Credit Consumption in Data 360

You can reduce the number of credits consumed by Data 360 data services by updating settings on

features such as data streams, data transforms, identity resolution, and more. For most features,

reducing the amount of data processed or the frequency of processing reduces costs.

Review the billing considerations for these features to understand how they consume credits and how to

refine your settings to reduce credit consumption.

•  Billing Considerations for Data Ingestion
•  Billing Considerations for Data Federation
•  Billing Considerations for Data Transforms
•  Billing Considerations for Identity Resolution
•  Billing Considerations for Insights
•  Billing Considerations for Segmentation
•  Billing Considerations for Predictive AI
•  Billing Considerations for Data Cloud Enrichments

After making updates to reduce consumption, you can use Digital Wallet to review your usage over time.

You can also build custom reports on Data 360 resource references to review usage of specific processes

within each feature.

•  About Digital Wallet
•  Data 360 Reportable Resource References

Some Salesforce CRM features are powered by Data 360 data. These features impact Data Services

Data Cloud License Billing and Limits

Adding a Data Cloud license enables Data 360 on a Salesforce org. Orgs with this license purchase

consumption credits which are consumed by use of Data 360 services.

Depending on when you purchased or renewed your Data Cloud license, your org consumes either Data

Services credits or Flex Credits for Data 360 services. Review Digital Wallet to determine which type of

credits apply to you.

Flex Credits Billable Usage Types for Data 360

Usage of certain Data 360 features impacts credit consumption. To monitor your usage in Flex Credits

usage categories, access your org’s Digital Wallet. If your org has a Data 360 Profiles-type license, some

usage types aren't consumed. For more information on how usage is billed, refer to your contract or

contact your account executive.

Data Services Billable Usage Types for Data 360

Usage of certain Data 360 features impacts credit consumption. If you purchased credits before

February 24, 2026, your org consumes Data Services credits for Data 360 services. Orgs purchasing or

renewing after February 24, 2026 can have either Data Services or Flex Credits. To monitor your usage

in these Data Servuces usage categories, access your org’s Digital Wallet. If your org has a Data 360

Profiles-type license, some usage types aren't consumed. For more information on how usage is billed,
refer to your contract or contact your account executive.

Data 360 Limits and Guidelines

Guidelines define best practice recommendations to optimize your adoption of Data 360 for best

performance. Limits are boundaries beyond which features are unavailable, performance is throttled,

or usage billing charges are applied. Since Data 360 is built to scale, some limits can be adjusted to

meet your business needs. Work with your account executive to find a solution that meets your goals.

•  If your org operates Data 360 under a Customer Data Platform license, refer to Customer Data

Platform Billable Usage Calculations instead.

•  If your org operates under a Data Cloud license and has an active Data Services consumption card,
refer to Data Services Billable Usage Types for Data 360 instead. If you also have a Data 360 Profiles

license, some usage is unmetered. Refer to Data 360 License Billing Considerations for details.
•  If your org operates Data 360 under a Data Cloud license but doesn’t have an active Data Services

consumption card, this article describes how credits are consumed.

The number of credits consumed is based on the number of units of each usage type used multiplied by

the multiplier listed on the rate card for the usage type.

Actual usage is summed for each usage type and credits are decremented at a fractional rate. The

minimum number of credits decremented from a usage type is 1, where fractional usage amounts to 1

or more credits over the monthly billing period.

Data 360 Profiles Licenses

If a Data 360 Profiles or Data 360 Enterprise Profiles license is added to your Data 360 org, some features

stop consuming credits. Refer to Data 360 Profiles License Billing and Limits for more details or review

the feature’s Billing Considerations article.

Data 360 Queries

Data 360 Unstructured

Processing

Usage is calculated based on the number of records processed.

The count of records processed depends on the structure of a query

as well as other related factors such as the total number of records

in the objects being queried.

When an object is queried in the context of a data space, the

number of rows processed is based on the total number of

processed rows in the source object, not the number of rows

pertaining to the particular data space

Usage is calculated based on the amount of unstructured data that

is processed without using AI assisted content processing and

extraction. For example, if the search index processes 100 PDF

documents that are 1 MB each, usage is calculated as 100 MB. If

the search index processes five audio/video files that are on average

100MB each, usage is calculated as 500MB.

In Data Cloud, unstructured data may be chunked and vectorized

using an embedding model. Usage is computed only once across

both these activities. For example, if one 100 MB PDF document is

chunked and vectorized, usage is computed as 100 MB, not as

200MB.If you create a search index that uses a data model object

(DMO) as a data source and select Text data type fields from the

DMO, all strings from those fields are indexed and the sum total of

all bytes processed is reported as Unstructured Data Processed.

Data 360 Intelligent Processing

Usage is calculated based on the amount of unstructured data that

is processed using AI-assisted features such as LLM-based parsing,

LLM-based visual data preprocessing, image processing, and

Intelligent Context.

Data 360 Streaming Pipeline

Usage is calculated based on the data object type.

For streaming data ingestion, usage is calculated based on the

number of rows of streaming data processed by Data 360 across all

data streams with stream processing, with the exception of

structured data that is ingested via the Internal Data Pipeline.

Data streams that report usage with this usage type are streams

created by Website and Mobile App Connector and streaming

ingestion API.

Data 360 Real-Time Pipeline

For streaming data transforms and streaming calculated insights,

usage is calculated based on the number of records processed.

For streaming data actions, usage is calculated based on the

based on the number of new records created or updated in the

Usage is calculated based on the sum of the number of profile

events, engagement events, API calls, and data actions processed in

traffic and real-time ingestion API. Profile events, engagement

events, API calls, and data actions are processed in the real-time

layer if they are associated with a real-time data graph.

For example, if 3 profile events, 10 engagement events, 20 API calls,

and 5 data actions are processed during a particular billing period,

the total processed is 38.

Data Servuces usage categories, access your org’s Digital Wallet. If your org has a Data 360 Profiles-type

Data 360 Limits and Guidelines

Guidelines define best practice recommendations to optimize your adoption of Data 360 for best

performance. Limits are boundaries beyond which features are unavailable, performance is throttled, or

usage billing charges are applied. Since Data 360 is built to scale, some limits can be adjusted to meet

your business needs. Work with your account executive to find a solution that meets your goals.

Some limits and guidelines vary by edition or org type, such as when using Data 360 in a Developer org.

For limits and guidelines related to Data 360 in a Developer org, see Developer Edition Limits and

Guidelines for Data Cloud. Limits that aren't designated as hard limits indicate the point at which

exceeding the limit may negatively impact performance, functionality, or usability. Hard limits, on the

other hand, can't be exceeded in a regularly provisioned org. Contact your Account Executive to request

an increase of the hard limit where indicated.

For limits related to Data 360 Reports, see Data 360 Reports and Dashboards: Limits and Limitations.

Note Some limits, guidelines, and usage billing calculations differ depending on your org’s

license.For billing information, refer to this additional document if your Data 360 org is operating

under a Data Cloud license.

•  Data Services Billable Usage Types for Data 360

Refer to these documents instead if your Data 360 org is operating under a Customer Data Platform

license.

•  Customer Data Platform Limits and Guidelines
•  Customer Data Platform Billable Usage Calculations

Contact your account executive if you aren’t sure which documents apply to you.

When creating an S3 data stream,

you may need to use a file smaller

than the data you’d like to ingest. The

smaller file should contain the same

headers and about 1,000 rows. Once

the data stream is created, larger files

can be placed within the file path,

maintaining that they fall within set

limits.

Sometimes, particularly for Day 0

loads, it’s necessary to move large

data volumes. The two parameters

maximum file size and maximum

files per scheduled run aren’t

intended to be stretched to their

respective maximums concurrently.

Rather consider some tradeoffs

between the two extremes and refer

to the other limit guidelines for more

context.

Compressed CSV files aren’t

splittable, meaning that they don't

allow for parallel processing and their

usage is therefore discouraged. If

sending in a compressed file, it must

be a single file per zip.

We recommend you to use the

parquet compression capabilities to

reduce file size.

Compressed parquet files are

splittable and support parallel

processing of ingestion. There are

several native compression options.

Learn more about supported

compression formats in Supported

File Formats in Data 360.

When a data stream is on upsert, it’s

best not to exceed a 50-GB aggregate

across all files in the single run. This

number is strongly influenced by the

number of distinct data dates

present in the table, the overall size

of the table, and several other factors

such as the number of columns. As

these variable inputs increase you

may experience performance

degradation.

For larger target tables and larger

upsert ingestions, we strongly

recommend using engagement

tables and selecting an engagement

date field that contains many distinct

dates. Not using engagement nor

selecting a high cardinality date field

may cause performance degradation.

Data size is the sum of all file sizes for

a single datastream job. When a data

stream is set for full refresh, it’s best

not to exceed 1000 GB for all files in

a single run. This number is strongly

influenced by the number of distinct

data dates present in the table, the

overall size of the table, and several

other factors such as the number of

columns. As these input variables

increase you may experience

performance degradation.

manually whenever you want.

instantly for active sessions. The

data graph refreshes every 1 hour.

graph impacts data graph refresh

times and query response times.

of the data graph exceeds 200 KB.

This can affect refresh times and

query response speeds.

this limit.

This limit is enforced in the UI.

All profile records processed by all

active rulesets are summed when

calculating billable usage. To avoid

excess credit consumption, we

recommend deleting unneeded

rulesets.

Because the time of day can vary,

ruleset jobs can occasionally run

more than once in a 24-hour period.

Scheduled ruleset jobs are skipped if

there are no changes to source data,

object mappings, or ruleset

configurations. This limit is enforced

automatically and isn't configurable.

Ruleset jobs don’t run if there are no

changes to source data, object

mappings, or ruleset configurations,

or if you’ve already run 4 ruleset jobs

in the last 24 hours.

Large profiles usually result from poor

data quality or match rules that are

too broad. To reduce the number of

matching records, clean your data or
refine your match rules.

Records that are larger than 15 KB are

skipped when rulesets run.

Data 360 Profiles License Billing and Limits

Data 360 Profiles and Data 360 Enterprise Profiles licenses can be added on to Data Cloud licenses to

change how a Data 360 org is billed and limited. When a Data 360 org has this license, its identity

resolution rulesets, profiles, segments, data transforms, and insights are limited but don't consume

credits.

Data 360 Profiles License Billing Considerations

Adding a Data 360 Profile or Data 360 Enterprise Profile license to a Data 360 org changes its

consumption billing and adds limits for certain features.

Data 360 Profiles License Base License Limits

Limits in this document represent the base limits of a single Data 360 Profiles or Data 360 Enterprise

Profiles license. Some limits can be raised by purchasing multiple copies of the license or buying add-

on licenses.

See Also

Salesforce Help: Data 360 Editions and Licenses

226

Data 360

Data 360 Licenses, Billing, and Limits

Data 360 Profiles License Billing Considerations

Adding a Data 360 Profile or Data 360 Enterprise Profile license to a Data 360 org changes its

consumption billing and adds limits for certain features.

All limits associated with Data 360 Profiles licenses apply to the production Data 360 home org and its

connectioned Data Cloud One companion orgs collectively. Sandbox orgs created from the Data 360

home org inherit the home org's limits. Limits apply to the sandbox org and its connected companion

orgs collectively. To review limits for orgs with Data 360 Profiles licenses, see Data 360 Profiles License

Base License Limits.

Profiles

The number of profiles included in your Data 360 org cluster is based on how many Data 360 Profile

licenses you purchase. If you exceed your profile entitlement, you’re charged at your overage rate.

For production orgs, if identity resolution is active in a data space, the count of profiles in each data

space is the sum of the total number of known unified profiles, the total number of anonymous unified

profiles, and the total number of records in all DLOs mapped to DMOs categorized as Profile that aren’t

used by identity resolution.

If identity resolution isn’t active, the billable profile count is the sum of all records in all data lake objects

(DLOs), regardless of category, mapped to data model objects (DMOs) categorized as Profile type,

excluding certain DMOs.

For sandbox orgs, the same counting logic applies, but the total number of profiles counted toward the

limit is 80% of the sum of all profiles in all data spaces on the sandbox org.

For a more detailed explanation of how profiles are counted, see Data 360 Profiles License Billable

Profiles Calculations.

Identity Resolution Rulesets

For production and sandbox orgs, rulesets are limited per data space.

Credits aren’t consumed by the Batch Profile Unificiation usage type when identity resolution runs.

Data Transforms

Credits aren’t consumed by the Batch Data Transforms usage type, but the total number of active batch

data transforms in your Data 360 org cluster is limited.

For production orgs, the number of batch data transforms counted toward the limit is the sum of all data

transforms in all data spaces on the home production org.

For sandbox orgs, the number of batch data transforms counted toward the limit is the sum of all data

227

Data 360

Data 360 Licenses, Billing, and Limits

transforms in all data spaces on the sandbox org.

Calculated Insights

Credits aren’t consumed by the Batch Calculated Insights usage type, but the total number of active

batch calculated insights in your Data 360 org cluster is limited.

For production orgs, the number of batch calculated insights counted toward the limit is the sum of all

calculated insights in all data spaces on the home production org.

For sandbox orgs, the number of batch calculated insights counted toward the limit is the sum of all

calculated insights in all data spaces on the sandbox org.

Segmentation

Credits aren’t consumed by the Segmentation usage type, but the total number of active segments

(including standard, waterfall and real-time types) in your Data 360 org cluster is limited.

For production orgs, the number of segments counted toward the limit is the sum of all segments in all

data spaces on the home production org and all segments in all data space on all connected Data Cloud

One Companion orgs.

For sandbox orgs, the number of segments counted toward the limit is the sum of all segments in all

data spaces on the sandbox org.

All Other Features

Activations: Credits aren’t consumed by the Batch Activation usage type, but the total number of active

batch activations on DMOs in your Data 360 org cluster is limited. Streaming DMO activations consume

credits.

Data Ingestion: Credits aren’t consumed when data is ingested via an internal data pipeline from a

Salesforce org or via a batch data connection from an external source. Streaming data ingestion
consumes credits.

Zero Copy Data Federation: Data federation via live queries and data federation via file federation don’t

consume the Data Federation or Sharing Rows Accessed usage type. This usage type is still consumed by

data sharing. Data federation with acceleration doesn’t consume the Batch Data Ingestion usage type.

AI Inferences: AI inferences don’t consume the Inferences usage type.

Data transforms, identity resolution, insights, and segments: These features continue to consume
supplementary usage types listed in their Billing Considerations, such as Data Queries and data storage.

All Other Features: All other features continue to consume credits at the regular rates as referenced in

the Data Services Billable Usage Types for Data 360and the features’ Billing Considerations.

Data 360 Licenses, Billing, and Limits

Data 360 Profiles License Billable Profiles Calculations

In orgs with a Data 360 Profiles license, the billable number of profiles is based on whether you have

active Identity Resolution rulesets. You’re billed at your overage rates for additional profiles if the

number of billable profiles exceeds your entitlement.

See Also

Salesforce Help: Data 360 Billable Usage Types

Data 360 Profiles License Billable Profiles Calculations

In orgs with a Data 360 Profiles license, the billable number of profiles is based on whether you have

active Identity Resolution rulesets. You’re billed at your overage rates for additional profiles if the number

of billable profiles exceeds your entitlement.

Counting Profiles in Data Spaces with Active Identity Resolution Rulesets

If you’re using identity resolution to link source profiles to Unified Profiles, the billable unified profile

count is the sum of your known unified profiles, 20% of your anonymous profiles, and of you source

profiles that aren’t used in identity resolution.

•  Known Unified Profiles: The number of known Unified Profile records output by active identity

resolution rulesets. To determine how many known Unified Profile records you have, view the Identity

Resolution Summary for each active ruleset. Add the number of known Unified Profiles across all

active rulesets.

•  Anonymous Unified Profiles: 20% of the number of anonymous unified profile records output by

active identity resolution rulesets. To calculate this number, view the Identity Resolution Summary for

each active ruleset. Multiply the number of anonymous profiles by 0.2. Add the number of anonymous

unified profiles across all active rulesets.

•  Ununified Source Profiles: The number of all records in all DLOs, regardless of category, that are

mapped to DMOs categorized as Profile, excluding Unified data model objects (Unified DMOs) output

by an identity resolution ruleset.

Counting Profiles in Data Spaces without Active Identity Resolution Rulesets

In a data space that isn’t using identity resolution, the billable profile count is the sum of all records in all

data lake objects (DLOs), regardless of category, mapped to data model objects (DMOs) categorized as

Profile type. Both known and unknown profile records are counted.

DLOs that are mapped only to the following DMOs are excluded from this count.

•  Account Contact
•  Contact Point Address
•  Contact Point App
•  Contact Point Consent
•  Contact Point Email

229

Data 360

Data 360 Licenses, Billing, and Limits

•  Contact Point OTT Service
•  Contact Point Phone
•  Contact Point Social
•  Device
•  Party Identification

Example Suppose your org has two identity resolution rulesets: Unified Individual.1 with 10,000

records and Unified Individual.2 with 8,000 records. There are also two DLOs that are categorized as

Profile and mapped to other DMOs that are categorized as Profile: the Account DLO has 2,000

records, and the Custom DLO has 5,000 records. For this customer, the total billable Unified Profiles

is 10,000 + 8,000 + 2,000 + 5,000 = 25,000.

Factors That Affect Unified Profile Counts

Address these factors to ensure that your profile counts accurately reflect your business needs.

Multiple Identity Resolution Rulesets

Unified profile counts from all active identity resolution rulesets are used to calculate total billable known

and anonymous profiles. Validate the number of active identity resolution rulesets. If more than one is

active, determine if all are needed for an active business purpose.

Data Stream Growth

As you connect different source systems to Data Cloud and increase the volume of data ingested through

new data streams, the number of source profiles increases. Review all data streams and sources

categorized as Profile. Determine if any duplicate, dev, test, or staging sources are connected and

whether they’re still needed.

Data Model Object Category

Data lake objects (DLOs) mapped to data model objects (DMOs) that are categorized as Profile are

available to segment on and are included in the Unified Profile count. Review all mappings from DLOs to
DMOs. Determine if all data streams mapped to DMOs categorized as Profile contain a population that

you want to segment by or use as the starting population for a segment. Determine if any DMOs are

categorized incorrectly as Profile.

If a DMO is categorized incorrectly as Profile, you can change its category to Other. You can change a

DMO’s category only if it isn’t used in segmentation or activation. Delete all segments and activations

that use the DMO before changing the category from Profile to Other. See Change the Category of a Data

Model Object.

Additional Unified Profile Count Considerations

•  Records in a DLO that is included in multiple data spaces are only counted once. The number of
records in the source DLO is counted, regardless of how many records are included in data space-
specific views of the DLO.

230

Data 360

Data 360 Licenses, Billing, and Limits

•  Data created from a transform that is output as an unmapped DMO isn’t counted toward billable

Unified Profiles. If a DLO isn’t mapped, it doesn’t count.

•  A DLO that is mapped to the Individual DMO and also to a DMO of type Profile isn’t counted twice.
•  All DLOs that are mapped to a DMO with type Profile count toward billable Unified Profiles. This count

includes these scenarios.
-
Data streams outside of identity resolution counts
-
Consent DMOs outside of identity resolution counts
-
Data transform or stream transform DLOs mapped to DMOs of type Profile outside of identity
resolution counts

See Also

Salesforce Help: Data 360 Billable Usage Types

Data 360 Profiles License Base License Limits

Limits in this document represent the base limits of a single Data 360 Profiles or Data 360 Enterprise

Profiles license. Some limits can be raised by purchasing multiple copies of the license or buying add-on

licenses.

Data 360 Profile Limits on Data Cloud One Companion Orgs and Sandbox
Orgs

Data Cloud One Org Companion Orgs: Batch calculated insights and segments created on companion

orgs are counted toward the Data 360 home org’s limit.

For example, if the home org purchases the base Data 360 Profiles license without any add-ons, it’s

limited to 25 batch calculated insights. If the home org has 20 batch calculated insights and the

companion org has 5 batch calculated insights, the org cluster has hit its limit of 25 batch calculated

insights.

Data 360 Sandboxes: Each sandbox org created from the production Data 360 home org inherits the

limits of its parent org. Identity resolution rulesets, batch data transforms, batch calculated insights, and
segments on the Data 360 sandbox org and its connected companion orgs are counted toward the Data

360 sandbox org’s limit.

On sandbox orgs, the number of profiles counted toward the profile limit is calculated by multiplying the

number of profiles by the weight. For example, if a production org has 100 unified profiles with a weight

of 1, then 100 unified profiles times 1 is counted as 100 unified profiles (100 x 1 = 100 profiles). A

sandbox org’s profiles have a weight of 0.8. Therefore, 100 profiles on a sandbox are counted as 80

profiles (100 x 0.8 = 80).

Customer Data Platform License Billing and Limits

Customers with this license have access to Data 360 on a Salesforce org. This license is no longer

available for purchase and can't be renewed. Orgs with this license are billed based on the numbers of

profiles, engagements, and other records in their orgs. Other features have limits. Not all Data 360

features are available on Data 360 orgs with this license.

Migrate Users from a Customer Data Platform License to a Data Cloud License

When you add a Data Cloud license to an org that was previously operating Data 360 under a

Customer Data Platform license, the permission sets granted by the Customer Data Platform license

no longer grants access to Data 360. To provide users continued access to Data 360, you must assign

the permission sets associated with the Data Cloud license to your users.

Customer Data Platform Billable Usage Calculations

Previously named Customer Data Platform orgs are billed based on contracted entitlements.

Understanding which usage is included for billing helps you make data management decisions.

Customer Data Platform Limits and Guidelines

Guidelines define best practice recommendations to optimize the adoption of Data 360 by Customer

Data Platform customers for best performance. Limits are boundaries beyond which features are

unavailable, performance is throttled, or usage billing charges are applied. This article is about the

legacy Customer Data Platform license, which is no longer available for purchase.

Migrate Users from a Customer Data Platform License to a Data Cloud
License

When you add a Data Cloud license to an org that was previously operating Data 360 under a Customer

Data Platform license, the permission sets granted by the Customer Data Platform license no longer

grants access to Data 360. To provide users continued access to Data 360, you must assign the

permission sets associated with the Data Cloud license to your users.

Assign Permission Sets

1. 1.  Identify which Data Cloud permission sets are associated with the Data Cloud license.

2. 2.  Optionally, customize the standard permission sets granted by the Data Cloud license or create custom

permission sets from them.

3. 3.  Assign the permission sets granted by the Data Cloud license to users.

To automate the process, use User Access Policies to migrate permission sets for groups of users.

4. 4.  Remove the permission sets granted by the Customer Data Platform license.

To automate the process, use User Access Policies to migrate permission sets for groups of users.

Customer Data Platform Billable Usage Calculations

Previously named Customer Data Platform orgs are billed based on contracted entitlements.

Understanding which usage is included for billing helps you make data management decisions.

Important These billing usage calculations apply only to Data 360 orgs with Customer Data

Platform licenses. If your Data 360 org has a Data Cloud license, see Data Services Billable Usage

Types for Data 360 instead.

You’re billed for usage in the areas of Unified Profiles, Segment Publishes, and Engagement Events. Your
maximum usage in these areas is defined in your contract’s entitlement schedule. Overages are billed
monthly at contracted rates. Contact your account team if you have questions about your contract.

Calculating Billable Unified Profiles for Customer Data Platform Orgs

The billable number of profiles is based on whether you have active Identity Resolution rulesets. You’re

billed for additional Unified Profiles if the number of billable profiles exceeds your entitlement.

If you’re not using identity resolution, the billable profile count is the sum of all records in all data lake

objects (DLOs), regardless of category, mapped to data model objects (DMOs) categorized as Profile

type. Both known and unknown profile records are counted. DLOs that are mapped only to the following

DMOs are excluded from this count.

•  Account Contact
•  Contact Point Address
•  Contact Point App
•  Contact Point Consent
•  Contact Point Email
•  Contact Point OTT Service
•  Contact Point Phone
•  Contact Point Social
•  Device
•  Party Identification

If you’re using Identity Resolution to link source profiles to Unified Profiles, the billable Unified Profile

count is the sum of both of these factors.

•  The number of known Unified Profile records for all active identity rulesets. To determine how many

Unified Profile records you have, view the Identity Resolution Summary for each active ruleset. Locate

the number of Unified Profiles for the ruleset in the summary. Add the number of known Unified

Profiles across all rulesets.

•  The number of all records in all DLOs, regardless of category, mapped to DMOs categorized as Profile,
excluding DMOs that are part of Identity Resolution. These records are included in the count because

you can use them to create segments. DLOs that are mapped to Other type DMOs are counted as

Engagement Events and not as Unified Profiles.

Anonymous profile limits are based on your Salesforce edition. When you’re using Identity Resolution,

anonymous profiles are excluded from the billable Unified Profile count.

Example This example has two active identity resolution rulesets: Unified Individual.1 with 10,000

records and Unified Individual.2 with 8,000 records. There are two DLOs that are categorized as

has 5,000 records. For this customer, the total billable Unified Profiles is 10,000 + 8,000 + 2,000 +

5,000 = 25,000.

Factors That Affect Unified Profile Counts for Customer Data Platform Orgs

Address these factors to ensure that your profile counts accurately reflect your business needs.

Multiple Identity Resolution Rulesets

Unified Profile counts from all active identity resolution rulesets are used to calculate total billable

profiles. Validate the number of active identity resolution rulesets. If more than one is active, determine

if all are needed for an active business purpose.

Data Stream Growth

As you connect different source systems to Data 360 and increase the volume of data ingested through

new data streams, the number of profiles increases. Review all data streams and sources categorized as

Profile. Determine if any duplicate, dev, test, or staging sources exist and whether they’re still needed.

Anonymous Profiles

Anonymous profiles don’t count toward billable Unified Profiles, but they must be marked as anonymous

when they’re ingested. Validate that the Is Anonymous field on the Individual DMO is correctly mapped

for any data stream that includes anonymous records.

DLOs mapped to DMOs categorized as Profile are available to segment on and are included in the

DMOs categorized as Profile contain a population that you want to segment by or use as the starting

population for a segment. Determine if any DMOs are categorized incorrectly as Profile.

If a DMO is categorized incorrectly as Profile, you can change its category to Other. You can change a

DMO’s category only if it isn’t used in segmentation or activation. Delete all segments and activations

that use the DMO before changing the category from Profile to Other. See Change the Category of a Data

Note Changing the Individual DMO can impact identity resolution.

•  Data created from a transform that is output as an unmapped DMO isn’t counted toward billable

•  A DLO that is mapped to the Individual DMO and also to a DMO of type Profile isn’t counted twice.
•  All DLOs that are mapped to a DMO with type Profile count toward billable Unified Profiles. This count

includes these scenarios.
-
Data streams outside of identity resolution counts
-
Consent DMOs outside of identity resolution counts

Data transform or stream transform DLOs mapped to DMOs of type Profile outside of identity
resolution counts

Calculating Segment Publishes for Customer Data Platform Orgs

Your Segment Publish entitlement is the maximum number of billable segment publishes during your

contract period.

Each time a segment is published, it counts as one billable segment publish. If a segment has more than

one activation or no activation associated with it, a single publication of that segment is counted as one

segment publish operation. Segment publishes that are completed during the time period are summed

and counted toward your entitlement.

To estimate your billable segment publication counts, review all publish schedules for all segments.

Calculating Engagement Events for Customer Data Platform Orgs

Your Engagement Events are calculated by summing all records in DLOs categorized as Engagement or

Other, so everything that doesn’t count as a Unified Profile record is counted as an Engagement Event.

Profile type DLOs that are mapped to Other type DMOs are also counted. You’re billed if your number of
records exceeds your entitlement.

To calculate the number of billable records, go to the Data Lake Object home page. Sum the record

counts of all DLOs except the ones that are mapped to a Profile type DMO because these DLOs are

counted as Unified Profiles. An unmapped DLO counts for Engagement entitlement but not for Unified

237

Profile entitlement.

For example, if a purchase record is copied from a source DLO to a target DLO using data transforms, the

record is counted as two Engagement Events because all records in both DLOs are part of the sum.

When creating an S3 data stream,

you may need to use a file smaller

than the data you’d like to ingest. The

smaller file should contain the same

headers and about 1,000 rows. Once

the data stream is created, larger files

can be placed within the file path,

maintaining that they fall within set

limits.

Sometimes, particularly for Day 0
loads, it’s necessary to move large

data volumes. Recommended limits

are: 200 GB max per file and 1,000

files max per scheduled run. These

two parameters aren’t intended to be

stretched to their respective

maximums concurrently. Rather

consider some tradeoff between the

two extremes and refer to the

maximum data size guidelines for

more context.

Compressed CSV files aren’t

splittable, meaning that they don't

allow for parallel processing and their
usage is therefore discouraged. If

sending in a compressed file, it must

be a single file per zip.

We recommend you to use the

parquet compression capabilities to

reduce file size.

Compressed parquet files are
splittable and support parallel

processing of ingestion. There are

several native compression options.

Learn more about supported

performance degradation.

API Guidelines and Limits

The concurrent request and query limits of Data 360 APIs are independent from the concurrency limits

governing the Salesforce platform APIs.

APIs: Query, Insights, and Profile

There are three distinct classes of APIs used to extract data: Profile, Query, and Calculated Insights. These

API limits for CDP orgs are based on the org’s Data 360 edition, not its Salesforce edition, except when

running Data 360 on a Developer org.

Data 360 Lifecycle Management

To manage your Data 360 lifecycle you can renew your license or delete your Data 360 instance to reset

the org. To keep your Data 360 instance, renew your license within the 120-day grace period. To set up a

new Data 360 instance with an active license, use the Data 360 cleanup process to delete its associated

data, metadata, and configurations. You can also use the cleanup process to connect your org as a Data

Cloud One companion to an existing Data 360 instance.

After you clean up the org, you can reset it in two ways:

•  Set up a new Data 360 instance that requires an active license.
•  Connect the org as a Data Cloud One companion to an existing Data 360 instance.

Renew an Existing Data 360 Instance

When a Data 360 license expires, it enters a 120-day grace period during which the Data 360 service is

deactivated but the data remains. Under this scenario, you can renew your license and restore your

current org. You also have the option to delete all Data 360 data.

Data 360 Cleanup and Reset

After the grace period ends and the license expires, the Data 360 tenant is deleted, but its data,

metadata, and configurations remain. To create a new Data 360 instance or to use it as a Data Cloud One

companion org, remove its data.

These are other scenarios for deleting all associated Data 360 data from an org.

•  To create a new Data 360 home org instance in the same or different region.
•  To convert an existing home org into a Data Cloud One companion org.
•  To connect your org as a Data Cloud One companion org to an existing Data 360 home org.
•  To set up an existing sandbox as a companion org for connected sandboxes.

264

Data 360

Data 360 Lifecycle Management

Cleaning up Data 360 data and metadata affects only the orgs directly connected to that Data 360

instance. When you clean up a Data 360home org on a sandbox to convert it into a companion org, this

action doesn’t impact any Data 360 features, data, metadata, or packages on the parent production org,

as the parent is connected to a different Data 360 instance.

Data 360 Data Deletion Process

The admin for the org follows the on-screen instructions in Data Cloud Setup to ensure all Data 360 data

and metadata are permanently removed from your org. If the org has expired or it contains Data 360

metadata and no Data 360 tenant, the Lifecycle Management screen displays.

Data Cloud Setup screen with a notification for expired licenses and orgs that have a disconnected

Data 360 tenant and leftover metadata.

Data Cloud Setup screen with a notification for expired licenses within the 120-day grace period.

265

Data 360

Data 360 Lifecycle Management

External Dependency Removal

External dependencies are configurations or features outside of Data 360 that rely on its functionality.

These include Data 360-triggered flows, copy field enrichments, and Agentforce Data Library. To continue

the data deletion process, first remove external dependencies. Navigate to each dependency to remove

it. After you remove all external dependencies, continue to approve the removal of unmanaged package

dependencies and any remaining data.

Remove External Dependencies screen with a Flow Definition to remove.

Unmanaged Package Dependencies Review

Unmanaged packages can contain both Data 360 and non-Data 360 objects. Allowing Salesforce to

remove the Data 360 objects doesn't affect unmanaged packages and any non-Data 360 objects they

266

Data 360

Data 360 Lifecycle Management

contain. Review how your objects are used to ensure there's no impact on your business needs and

processes. Data 360 managed packages are automatically removed as part of Data 360 cleanup.

Review Packaged Dependencies screen that displays a list of Data 360 objects to review before

approving deletion.

Data Deletion

After you review the list of unmanaged packages, grant approval for Data 360 to delete the remaining

data. Deleting all Data 360 data is a permanent process. After completion, you can no longer access the

following.

•  Data 360 features, data, metadata, data spaces, and packages
•  Data 360 functionality from any connected companion orgs

Salesforce can't provide a backup of customer data or restore your Data 360 instance.

After you approve, data deletion begins. This process can take up 50 minutes. After it’s finished, the Data

Cloud Setup screen refreshes.

Screen that displays the Data 360 cleanup process in progress.

267

Org Reset

The Data Cloud Setup screen displays options for how to reset your cleaned up org, based on your

license.

•  To create a home org, you need a home org license.
•  To create a Data Cloud One companion org, you need both home org and companion org licenses.

Initiate the companion org connection from a different, existing home org.

Users with an expired license or who no longer have a Data 360 tenant see this screen with

information about connecting to Data 360 upon completion of the cleanup process.

Einstein and Data Usage in Data 360

Einstein and Data Usage in Data 360

Einstein is built on data. When using Data 360, review this table to understand the type of data that

Einstein features use.

The table lists the Customer Data that is used, which is data submitted by the Customer to our services

as defined in our Main Services Agreement (MSA), and the usage data that is used, which is data relating

to users’ interactions with Salesforce. Data submitted to an Einstein feature may be used to train AI

models, to improve your services and features, or to develop new features that you can access without

additional cost.

The table also indicates which features use global models, which are models that look for aggregated,

anonymous trends across multiple Salesforce Customers. The Customer has control over whether their

data contributes to global models, if offered. For more details, see Data 360 Billable Usage Types and

Billing Considerations for Audit and Feedback.

Data 360

Data 360 setup is important in making your implementation a success. After provisioning Data 360, you

can capture, unify, segment, and activate your customer data. A user sometimes can inherit more than

one permission set to carry out several responsibilities.

Note As of October 14, 2025, Data Cloud has been rebranded to Data 360. During this transition,
you may see references to Data Cloud in our application and documentation. While the name is

new, the functionality and content remains unchanged.

Turn On Data 360

Data 360 is automatically provisioned as soon as a Data Cloud license is added to your Salesforce org.

However, if auto provisioning isn't available or if you’re working in a Developer Edition or sandbox org,

you must manually enable it. Data 360 can be enabled on a new or an existing Salesforce org.

Create Data 360 Users and Assign Permissions

Create users and provide access to Data Cloud features like identity resolution, transforms, and

calculated insights.

Manage Features and Connections

Grant and remove access to data explorer and external connections.

Data Source Configuration in Data 360

To connect data sources, review the admin tasks that must be completed first. After they’re configured

in Data Cloud Setup, data streams can be created for each data source. Find information about all the

varieties of data source connectors, their configuration, and data stream setup under Connect Data.

Data Target Configuration in Data 360

To configure data targets, review the admin tasks that must be completed first.

Enable Data 360 Features

You can enable Data 360 features using the Feature Manager. This screen is visible only when there are

one or more features to enable or disable.

General Set Up Tasks in Data 360

In addition to provisioning and connecting data sources, learn about additional tasks completed in

Data Cloud Setup.

To access Data Cloud Setup

System admin profile OR

Data Cloud Architect permission set

1. 1.  Go to Data Cloud Setup.

2. 2.  Under User Management, click Users.

3. 3.  Add new users or edit an existing user.

4. 4.  Select a user and click Permission Set Assignments.

5. 5.  Click Edit Assignments.

6. 6.  Select the appropriate Data Cloud permission set and click Add.

7. 7.  Click Save.

Repeat these steps for all users needing access to Data Cloud features.

Data 360 Standard Permission Sets

A permission set defines the level of access and visibility that Salesforce users have to data and

features in Data 360. Depending on your license, there several standard permission sets provided for

Data 360. The Salesforce admin assigns permission sets to users. We don’t recommend creating a

custom permission set for Data 360 access, however you can combine the permissions sets with other

Salesforce permission sets.

Custom Permission Sets in Data Cloud

To create a Data Cloud custom permission set, we recommend cloning an existing standard Data

Cloud permission set. Some Data Cloud features can’t be accessed with permission sets created from

scratch.

Migrate Data Cloud Permission Sets using User Access Policies

Learn how to use user access policies to grant updated Data Cloud permission sets to groups of users

based on criteria you set.

Manage Data Cloud Data Access Levels for Salesforce Users

You can configure permission sets to grant Salesforce users view access to related list enrichments or

other SOQL queries to Data Cloud data without granting access to Data Cloud or permission to view
Data Cloud in other contexts.

Data 360 Standard Permission Sets

A permission set defines the level of access and visibility that Salesforce users have to data and features

in Data 360. Depending on your license, there several standard permission sets provided for Data 360.

The Salesforce admin assigns permission sets to users. We don’t recommend creating a custom

permission set for Data 360 access, however you can combine the permissions sets with other Salesforce
permission sets.

Note As of Sept. 4, 2025, standard permission sets were updated. Please see the Data Cloud

Standard Permission Set Transition Guide to learn about the changes.

292

Data 360

Create Data 360 Users and Assign Permissions

About Permissions

In Salesforce, profile, permissions, and permission sets are fundamental aspects of user access. The best

practice is to set up a user with the minimum level of permissions that the user needs to do their job.

•  Profiles: Every Salesforce user is assigned to one profile. In addition to permissions, profiles control tab

visibility, page layout assignments, record type access, and IP ranges.

•  Permissions: Permissions determine whether a user can perform a particular action, such as read,

create, or edit for a specific object or feature.

•  Permission Sets: A permission set is a collection of permissions that grants additional access to users.

Users can have multiple permission sets assigned to them.

Admins can create custom permissions. However, Data Cloud standard permission sets are automatically

updated with each release as new features become available. By using a custom permission set could

result in users not having access to new features or functionality.

System Administrator Profile

To manage and assign users in Setup and access Data Cloud Setup, you can have a System Administrator

user profile or the permissions that grant access to Salesforce Setup, for example, customize applicaton.

You don't need a Data Cloud standard permission set to access Data Cloud Setup if you have a system

admin profile.

Note The Salesforce System Admin profile includes Manage All Data Space definition permission

which grants users access to all Data Spaces. If the default Allow All policy is active in the org,users

with the Sytem Admin profile can query all Data 360 DMOs. To preserve data security, we

recomment deleting the default Allow All policy or editing its scope to apply to specific users. See

Data Governance in Data 360 for more information.

Data Cloud Standard Permission Sets

You can combine these Data 360 permission sets with other Salesforce permission sets for users who

need additional access.

Data Cloud Architect (formerly known as Data Cloud Admin)—Users with this permission set can access

all functionality within Data 360, including Data Cloud Setup, mapping data to the data model, creating

data streams, identity resolution rulesets, and insights.

Feature Access:

•  Full Access: Data Spaces, Data Governance, Data Shares, Data Streams, DLOs, DMOs, Data Transforms,

Data Graphs, Query Editor, Identity Resolution, Insights, Data Actions, Data Action Targets,

Communication Capping, Segments, Activations, Activation Targets, Einstein Studio AI Models,

Unstructured Data Hub, Search Index, Semantic Layer

access to Setup functionality, clone this permisison set and remove this permission. See this article

for more information about this permission.

Data Cloud Activation Manager (formerly known as Data Cloud Marketing Manager)—Users with this

permission set can manage an overall segmentation strategy, including creating activation targets and

activations.

Feature Access:

Semantic Layer

•  No Access: Data Cloud Setup, Data Spaces, Data Governance, Data Shares, Einstein Studio AI Models,

Unstructured Data Hub, Search Index, Semantic Layer

Data Cloud User—Users with this permission set can view Data 360 features.

Feature Access:

•  Full Access: None
•  View Only Access: Data Spaces, Data Governance, Data Shares, Data Streams, DLOs, DMOs, Data
Transforms, Data Graphs, Query Editor, Identity Resolution, Profile Explorer, Insights, Data Actions,

Data Action Targets, Communication Capping, Segment, Activations, Activation Targets, Einstein

Studio AI Models, Unstructured Data Hub, Search Index, Semantic Layer

•  No Access: Data Cloud Setup

Legacy Permission Sets

The following permissions are now legacy permissions. While still available, we recommend transitioning

to new permissions sets to gain access to new features and enhancements.

•  Legacy Data Cloud Marketing Admin—Users with this permission set can manage day-to-day
configuration needs, support, maintenance, and perform regular internal system audits.

•  Legacy Data Cloud Data Aware Specialist—Users with this permission set can map data to the data

model and create data streams, identity resolution rulesets, and calculated insights.

Additional Permission Sets

Several features use permission sets to manage access. Review information regarding how permission

sets are used across Data 360.

•  Data Cloud Salesforce Connector—When you connect to an org, the Data Cloud Salesforce Connector

permission set is created to allow access to Data 360 objects and fields. See Salesforce CRM

Permissions and Enable Object and Field Permissions for CRM Connections.

•  Data-Space Aware—For data-space aware features, access granted by permission sets only applies to
associated data spaces. See Manage Feature Access for Data Space-Aware Data Cloud Features and

Associate a Permission Set with a Data Space.

•  Data Cloud One—Data Cloud One companion orgs don't use standard Data 360 permission sets. To
grant access to the Data Cloud One app on companion orgs, assign the Data Cloud One User

permission set. To refine access to features offered within the app, clone and edit the permission set.

Custom Permission Sets in Data Cloud

To create a Data Cloud custom permission set, we recommend cloning an existing standard Data Cloud

REQUIRED EDITIONS
REQUIRED EDITIONS

USER PERMISSIONS NEEDED

To clone permission sets:

Manage Profiles and Permission Sets

Custom permission sets aren’t automatically updated when Data Cloud features get new permissions,

even if they’re created by cloning a standard Data Cloud permission set.

When you clone a permission set, its data space associations are included in the new permission set.

When you create a permission set from scratch, you must manually associate it with a data space.

Add Object Permissions to Custom Permission Sets for Data 360

Object permissions for new Data Cloud objects are added to all standard Data Cloud permission sets
when the new objects is added. However, object permissions for new objects but must be manually

added to custom permission sets. Use these object permissions to update any custom Data Cloud

permission sets that were created before the new object was added to Data Cloud.

Add Object Permissions to Custom Permission Sets for Data 360

Object permissions for new Data Cloud objects are added to all standard Data Cloud permission sets

when the new objects is added. However, object permissions for new objects but must be manually
added to custom permission sets. Use these object permissions to update any custom Data Cloud

permission sets that were created before the new object was added to Data Cloud.

Manage Data Cloud Data Access Levels for Salesforce Users

You can configure permission sets to grant Salesforce users view access to related list enrichments or

other SOQL queries to Data Cloud data without granting access to Data Cloud or permission to view Data

Cloud in other contexts.

To update data access levels, in Setup, select the permission set and go to the Data Cloud Data Space

Management, then select a data space.

Grant Controlled by Parent Access to Data Cloud Data

Relationships between objects are referred to as “parent-child” relationships when one object (the

parent object) contains values used by another object (the child object).

Granting Controlled by Parent access on a data space lets users view data in a child object as long as they

have access to view the data in the related parent object. If you grant Controlled by Parent access to Data

Cloud data, Salesforce users can view Data Cloud data in related lists or SOQL query results as long as

they have permission to view the record the data is related to.

Example For example, assume Data Cloud ingests information about your contacts from the

Contact object in your Salesforce org. Your contact records and related records, such as engagement

records, are then processed by identity resolution and included in unified profiles. An system admin

creates an enriched related list on the Contact object that shows all the engagement data from the

unified profile for each contact. The admin wants to let users see the enriched related list data

without letting them access Data Cloud or view unified profiles directly. In this scenario, the admin

can give Controlled by Parent access to users who have permission to view Contact object records to

allow them to also view the enriched related list.

Set Up an External Activation Platform

Reach more customers by connecting an external activation platform to Data 360. Install an external

activation platform from AppExchange or a packaged URL.

REQUIRED EDITIONS
REQUIRED EDITIONS

Available in: All Editions supported by Data 360. See Data 360 edition availability.

USER PERMISSIONS NEEDED

To access Data Cloud Setup

System admin profile OR

Data Cloud Architect permission set

1. 1.  From Setup, select Data Cloud Setup.

2. 2.  Under External Integrations, select External Activation Targets.

3. 3.  Select the external activation platform.

Note Segment names are included in activations. To exclude segment names in the metadata file

sent to the external activation platform, turn off Include segment name in activations to this

platform.

4. 4.  To enable filtering by data privacy requirements, select the privacy type to indicate how your

customers are impacted by the California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA).
If your customers aren’t impacted by CPRA (see California Privacy Protection Agency), select Not

Applicable.

5. 5.  For ISV-created JSON-based External Activation platforms, review the ID Type Mapping tab. If the ISV

has configured supported IDs, update the ID Type field to map to the corresponding partner-

supported identifiers. Mapping ID types normalizes the ID type, ensuring records are activated to the
appropriate destination folder when the output is grouped by  PER_USER  (user identifier). The ID

Type values are case-sensitive. For example, map Google to GAID, GoogleId, or GId as comma-

separated values.

6. 6.  Save your changes.

7. 7.  Click Enable to use the platform for activations.

You can disable an external activation platform. However, activations associated with a disabled

platform won’t be processed.

315

Data 360

Data Target Configuration in Data 360

Considerations for External Activation Platforms Created by ISV Partners Using JSON

•  After mapping the ID values and including them in the activation definition's Contact Point Digital ID
filters, all records with these contact point filtering values are activated to the ISV partner’s S3 bucket

when the activation runs.

•  If an ISV partner discontinues support for an identifier during a package upgrade, you'll need to
update the activations to reflect the changes made by the ISV partner during the upgrade.

•  If you have mapped all possible values for the IDs supported by the ISV partner, and no additional

contact point digital Id filters are applied, all records in the Contact Point Digital Id DMO linked to the

supported identifiers are activated. However, applying filters allows for more control over which

records are included in the activation.

•

Note See Ingest and Model Digital Identifiers for JSON-based External Activation Targets to learn

how to model and map digital identifiers to the ContactPointDigitalId DMO to successfully use

the activation toolkit for external platforms.

Create a Microsoft Azure Container SAS Token

Container Shared Access Signature (SAS) tokens give access to files in your Microsoft Azure Storage

container.

To create SAS tokens:

1. 1.  Sign in to the Microsoft Azure portal and go to your Azure Storage account.

2. 2.  In your Microsoft Azure container, from Settings, click Shared access tokens.

3. 3.  Create a SAS token with these settings.
• •  Signing Method - Account Key
• •  Required Permissions - read, write, list, delete, tag. To add the tag permission, generate the token

using the Azure Storage Explorer app and follow the steps in Get the SAS for a blob container. Refer

to the See Also section for more information on the permissions supported for each resource type.

• •  Allowed Protocols - HTTPS only

4. 4.  Copy the Blob SAS Token and Blob SAS Url. They’re used in Set Up a Microsoft Azure Target

Connection

We recommend that you regenerate the SAS token before expiry to avoid invalid credential errors
when connecting to Data 360. Data 360 Azure Storage Service Connector doesn't support Azure

account or Azure file tokens.

See Also

External: Permissions for a directory, container, or blob

Data Cloud Queries and Fiscal Years

Data Cloud queries use the fiscal year set in Salesforce. However, the home org and each companion

org can set their own fiscal year. If an org doesn’t have a defined fiscal year, queries that include fiscal

data parts return results based on the Gregorian calendar, January 1 to December 31.

applies them to data transforms, calculated insights, segmentations, reports, and other processes.

Data Cloud Queries and Fiscal Years

Data Cloud queries use the fiscal year set in Salesforce. However, the home org and each companion org

can set their own fiscal year. If an org doesn’t have a defined fiscal year, queries that include fiscal data

parts return results based on the Gregorian calendar, January 1 to December 31.

Note Custom fiscal year isn't support for Data Cloud orgs.

Data Cloud queries group, sort, and filter your data model object (DMO) reports using the standard fiscal

week, month, year, or quarter. For example, to compare seasonal spending habits in a sales order DMO

report, group your customer spend by the standard fiscal quarter.

Only the  extract  and  date_trunc  query functions use the fiscal date fields. The other date

functions support only standard date fields. For example,  CreatedDate_Year  is a standard date field,

and  CreatedDate_Year_Fiscal  is a fiscal year field. Data Cloud queries generate fields for fiscal parts

and append the field with the  _Fiscal  suffix.

When updates are made to the fiscal calendar in Salesforce setup, the updates can take up to 24 hours

to show up in the Data Cloud org.

See Also

Salesforce Help: Set the Fiscal Year

Using Currencies in Data Cloud

Data Cloud uses the currencies and static exchange rates configured in your Salesforce CRM org and

applies them to data transforms, calculated insights, segmentations, reports, and other processes.

In a single-currency organization, Data Cloud syncs its currency data from your Salesforce org using this
process.

•  After the Salesforce CRM connector to Data Cloud is automatically set up, Salesforce creates a static
rate data lake object (DLO) named  Static_Currency_Rates_<CRM orgID>  and a static rate

conversion data model object (DMO) named  Static_Currency_Rates_<CRM orgID>  for the

currency data. If the CRM connector has an alias, then the alias replaces  <CRM orgID>  in the name.
•  The Salesforce CRM connector syncs active and inactive currencies and static conversion rates to the

associated currencies connection in Data Cloud.

•  When the Salesforce admin adds currencies or updates the conversion rate in a Salesforce CRM org,

Data Cloud syncs these changes, and the static rate conversion DMO is updated within a few minutes.

In a multiple-currency organization, Data Cloud uses the same process to sync its currency data from

each connected Salesforce org and follows a similar naming convention for the DLO and DMOs it

322

Data 360

General Set Up Tasks in Data 360

creates. In addition to the DLO and DMOs, Salesforce creates a data stream named
Static_CurrencyType_<CRM orgID> . Each CRM org manages its own currencies and conversion

rates.

Note We recommend not adding formula fields to the data stream.

•  If an org context is present for the Data Cloud query, Data Cloud uses the conversion rate from the org.

For example, Data Cloud applies the currency conversion rates from a logged-in user’s org when:
-
The user’s actions trigger queries on Data Explorer or Data Cloud reports
-
The user executes SQL or SOQL queries using an API

•  If an org context isn’t present for the Data Cloud query, Data Cloud applies the default conversion
rates. Examples include background and service processes such as data pipelines running data

transforms, segmentation, and activation.

•  Data Cloud applies these conversion rates.

Considerations for Using Multiple Currencies in Data Cloud

Keep these considerations in mind when using multiple currencies in Data Cloud.

Billing Considerations for Multi-Currency Usage

Using multiple currencies in Data Cloud impacts the consumption of credits used for orgs operating

Data Cloud under a Data Cloud license. Credits are consumed for setting up currencies and

maintaining them over time.

Review Currencies Connection Status in Data Cloud

If your Data Cloud org uses multiple currencies from your Salesforce CRM org, you can review the

associated connection’s status.

Disable a Currency Connection in Data Cloud

While we recommend keeping the currency connection in Data Cloud enabled, if you plan to

disconnect a standard Salesforce CRM connection from Data Cloud, disable the currency connection

to Data Cloud first.

Considerations for Using Multiple Currencies in Data Cloud

Keep these considerations in mind when using multiple currencies in Data Cloud.

323

Data 360

General Set Up Tasks in Data 360

•  Data Cloud supports only static conversion rates and ignores dated conversion rates that are enabled

in your Salesforce CRM org.

•  If a currency’s conversion rate isn’t specified in your Salesforce org, Data Cloud returns a null value for
the currency field. To avoid this issue, add currency conversion rates in your Salesforce org or use your

own conversion rate DMO.

You can test the conversion rate using the Data Cloud Query Service conversion function in the Query

Editor.

select Order_ID__c, Sales__c, try_convert_currency(Sales__c, 'USD', 'EUR') a

s Sales_EUR, Profit__c, cdp_sys_record_currency__c from orders_same_currenc

y__dll limit 10

•  If you connect multiple CRM orgs to Data Cloud, use the same list of currencies and conversion rates

in each org.

•  Data Cloud doesn’t support currency conversions across different CRM orgs connected to it. For

example, assume that Data Cloud syncs conversion rates for US dollars (USD) and euros (EUR) from

CRM org 1, and Japanese yen (JPY) and Indian rupee (INR) from CRM org 2. In this scenario, Data

Cloud doesn’t support these conversions: USD to JPY, USD to INR, EUR to JPY, and EUR to INR. To

avoid null values in your conversions, add USD and EUR currency rates to org 2, and JPY and INR

currency rates to org 1.

•  A currency field in a DMO can support different currencies. For example, the Amount field in a Sales
Order DMO can be in USD for one order and in EUR for another. To help with currency conversions in
such instances, the  cdp_sys_record_currency  field, which contains the ISO currency code value,

is included by default.

•  You can’t use a single-currency org in a sandbox org.

Keep these additional considerations in mind when using multiple currencies in calculated insights.

•  All currency fields in a calculated insight must be in the same currency. For example, if a calculated

insight includes two measures with currency values, all fields for both measures must be in the same

currency.

•  When using a calculated insight to aggregate currency values, the currency values must be converted

into a single currency.

•  When using the builder to create a calculated insight, the builder automatically manages the

conversion logic. But, the user must select the currency for the insight output.

•  When creating a calculated insight with currency fields using SQL, to adhere to syntax standards,

include the  try_convert_currency  function using this syntax:

try_convert_currency(Source Currency Field, Source Currency ISO, Target Curr

ency ISO)

•  When using the builder to create a calculated insight that includes the currency data type, the builder
automatically adds the  currency_type_c  field. When creating a calculated insight with currency

fields using SQL, the user must add this field manually.
