Segment Canvas

You can compute results with different similarity levels and different values as needed.

11. 11.  Click Done to save the filter.

The filter operates within its defined scope, making sure the data it collects is relevant and fits the

context you're looking for, thus improving the accuracy of your segment data.

Currency Data Type in Segmentation

You can use the currency data type to convert currency when performing aggregations and creating the

required groups in segmentation filters.

Make sure that the default currency conversion data model object (DMO) includes all required

conversion rates. This ensures accurate results. If the conversion rates are missing from the currency

conversion DMO, you could get incorrect results.

Note The currency data type is not currently supported in segments created using API.

Currency Attribute in Filters

You can segment your data by using the currency data type attribute. When creating a filter, you select a

currency code from the currency dropdown menu. This currency code is used to normalize the data.

Example

If your filter condition is Order Total = $500 and the Income attribute contains values in multiple

currencies, all values are converted to USD (the currency selected in the filter), using the currency

conversion DMO. After the conversion, the filter condition is applied to the segment.

Note There can be some mismatch between the segment count and segment publish results when

a filter currency field is used.

Currency Attribute in Aggregations

When performing aggregation operations such as sum or average with a currency attribute, you select a

currency code from the currency dropdown menu. This currency code is used to normalize the data

before carrying out the aggregations.

1521

Data 360

Segment Canvas

Note

•  No implicit currency conversion occurs as part of any other operation.
•  Rounding errors during currency conversions can sometimes lead to inaccurate results in

segmentation.

Approximate Segment Population

When building a segment in Data 360, use the Approximate Segment Population field to quickly check

that the segment count meets your expectations. The approximate count provides an estimated

segment population, represented as a range of possible values with 95% confidence. When the

segment population is small, or when the record count for Segment On is low, the actual population can

differ from the estimated range. You can then adjust your segment rules and save your segment to get

the final segment population. To use this feature, enable Approximate Segment Population in Feature

Manager.

To calculate the Approximate Segment Population, we use a subset of your profile dataset, compute

filters on this dataset, count the population, and then normalize this data against the sampling

percentage. This calculation provides an estimate of the segment population, which is a range of

possible population values at a 95% confidence level.

Note

•  Approximate count works with zero copy, except when the profile data being segmented on is
itself external. In that case, we fall back to the exact count instead of the approximate count.
•  When approximate segment Population is enabled, filter level and container level counts also

return approximate count.

Segment Time Zone

Segment publish schedules are interpreted in the user’s time zone. Your Data 360 org sets the publish

time zones on the initial segment save and segment canvas. Segment and activation fields display the

Publish Schedule Start Date and Time in the user's time zone.

The Salesforce org time zone still applies to other segmentation behavior, such as date-based operators

like Last 'n' Days.

Updates made to your Salesforce org’s time zone aren’t reflected in existing segments.

Example You schedule the segment publish start time for 1:00 PM EST (UTC-5) with a 24-hour

interval. That same absolute time is 10:00 AM PST (UTC-8). If the Salesforce org time zone is later

changed from EST to PST, the publish still occurs at the same absolute instant, so it appears as

10:00 AM PST, not 1:00 PM PST.

Newly created segments follow the updated time zone. To update the time zone of an existing segment,
resave the segment.

Note The save action is triggered only when specific payload fields change. A change to any one of

these fields triggers a segment update request: Name, Description, Include Criteria, Exclude

Criteria, Publish Schedule Start Date and Time, Publish Schedule Interval, Publish Schedule End

1529

Data 360

Segment Canvas

Date, Publish Schedule Info, or Lookback Period. A change to the time zone alone doesn't trigger an

update.

Segment publish is scheduled based on a time interval (for example, 12 or 24 hours) rather than a

specific date and time. Therefore, a segment publish time doesn’t adjust for DST.

See Also

Salesforce Help: Change Time Zones

Use Value Suggestions in Segmentation

You can enable value suggestions for data model object (DMO) fields if the data type is Text. Enable or

deactivate the feature in the DMO record home. You can enable value suggestions for up to 500

attributes for your entire org. It can take up to 24 hours for suggested values to appear.

1. 1.  In Data 360, click the Segments tab.

2. 2.  Select a segment.

3. 3.  To use value suggestion when creating segment filters, drag the attribute onto the canvas.

4. 4.  Start typing in the Value field for an attribute.

If you don’t see the values in your list yet, start typing the values you’ve already ingested or type values

exactly as they appear in your dataset.

Suggested values are retained for 30 days in the suggested values dataset. For attributes with more

than 1,000 values, the most frequently occurring 1,000 values in the dataset are displayed

alphabetically. This includes both new and old suggested values. Some operators allow you to select

multiple values for an attribute. Values with more than 255 characters aren’t available as suggested

values, but you can still type them in to filter on them.

Note When suggested values are enabled on fields mapped to external objects (See BYOL),

charges apply per field every 24 hours.

1530

Segment Canvas

Note
• •  When the DMO's category is Other, value suggestion is available when the relationships from

the Segment On entity to the DMO are one-to-one (1:1) and many-to-one (N:1). Value

suggestions aren’t available when the relationships are one-to-many (1:N). The DMO category

and relationships are determined while ingesting and mapping your data.

• •  Use data newer than 30 days. If the data has been inactive for 30 days, the values don’t appear.

Multiple Identity Resolution Rulesets in Segments

Compare the impact of different identity resolution rulesets for the same entity on segment population

counts. After using identity resolution to create different rulesets for the same entity, entities and

attributes created by both rulesets are available in segmentation. Use attributes from both rulesets to

validate, or A/B test, different population counts. Entities and attributes names include the Ruleset ID at

the end when you select what entity to Segment On or add attributes in the attribute library.

Use Identity Resolution to create two different rulesets for the Individual entity. For the first ruleset, use
strict match rules. For the second ruleset, use more general match rules and add Ruleset ID fzzy. To

build a new segment based on the fzzy ruleset, Segment On Unified Individual fzzy.

1531

Data 360

Troubleshoot Segment Errors

Tip Use the second ruleset as a temporary way to create the best ruleset for your data, and then

delete the second ruleset. Unified profiles from all rulesets count toward your entitlement limit.

Multiple Marketing Cloud Engagement Business Units in Segments

Filter segments by business unit (BU) to determine the true size of segments for campaign planning. If

segments aren’t filtered by business unit, the difference between a Data 360 segment population and

Marketing Cloud Engagement data extension count can be significant.

•  In Data 360 Setup, make sure that Allow Profile Business Unit Mapping Data is enabled.

1. 1.  For new and existing segments, add another rule.
2. 2.  Select the Affiliation entity from the attribute library under Related Attributes.

3. 3.  Drag the Affiliated To attribute to the segmentation canvas.

4. 4.  Use an Is Equal To operator and enter a Business Unit Value (MID) for the segment.

Troubleshoot Segment Errors

Troubleshooting Suggestions

•  Use a Calculated Insight (CI) to reduce the

number of DLOs referenced by your segment.
•  Split a segment into multiple smaller segments.

•  Use a CI instead of many attributes and nested

operators.

•  Use a CI instead of an attribute (data model

object) with many relationships.

•  Combine text values into one  Is In  text

operator.

•  Remove placeholder values like 0 or Unknown
from source data before ingesting data into

Data 360.

•  Copy the inactive segment to create a segment

with the same population.

•  Wait for some segments to finish publishing

and try again.

•  Change the publish schedule for some of your

segments.

•  Wait for the recount to finish and try publishing

the segment again.

Segment wasn’t processed.

•  Contact Salesforce Customer Support for help.

Multiple population counts are in progress.

•  Wait for the counts to complete and try again.
•  Improve the segment by making it simpler,
using nested segments, or merging the
containers, if possible.

1533

Data 360

Error

Segment population count failed.

Segment can’t be published.

Segment count/population mismatch.

Troubleshoot Segment Errors

Troubleshooting Suggestions

•  Identify containers with the same join paths
and merge them using nested operators, if

possible.

•  Avoid long paths and use the shortest join path

to reach the needed attribute.

•  Avoid cyclic paths in segments. Cyclic paths are
relationships that use cyclic behavior (a→b→a).
While segment counts can fail, segment jobs

can run successfully.

•  Simplify your segment by merging containers
when possible. Use nested operators to merge

the containers.

•  Ensure the DMO types are correct, especially for
Engagement Type data. Incorrect DMO types

can cause timeouts and failures.

•  Segmentation applies a filter on the

engagement date (24 months for standard

segments and 7 days for rapid segments). In

Data Explorer, make sure to apply the filter on

the engagement event date.

•  Ensure date operators match with tenant

timezones.

•  Check if the source data has drastically changed
(significant additions, updates, or deletions).
•  If you use Calculated Insights in your segments
and notice an unexpected increase or decrease
in segment count or segment population, check

if any Identity Resolution rules were processed

between the CI and segment run.

•  Segmentation in Data 360 generates a list of
unique profile IDs as output. But Marketing

Cloud uses the Subscriber Key attribute for

segmentation; hence, the population counts in

Data 360 and Marketing Cloud can differ.

Unable to edit segment, or segment editor UI

times out.

Einstein Segments in Data 360

Create segments with Einstein Segment Creation generative AI. Enter a high-level description of your

segment and receive a suggested segment and all its attributes. Easily draft another segment by

changing the description, or edit the segment’s attributes to make adjustments. After you’re satisfied

with your segment, publish and activate it.

Einstein Segments and Your Data

When you generate a segment, Salesforce doesn’t send Personally Identifiable Information (PII) data,

including data from the Unified Individual DMO, to third-party sources. Your customer data isn’t shared

with others or used to enrich other customer data. For more information, see Data Masking.

Salesforce sends sample data for each field so that generative AI can understand the context and create

a grounded model. For example, if a Hobby field exists in your data, the grounded model can recognize

that hiking, canoeing, and running are related to hobbies. Generative AI can then suggest meaningful
segment definitions that relate to your actual audience data when you enter a description, such as

customers who enjoy outdoor sports.

Trust and Einstein Segments

Unethical or biased language isn’t allowed when creating an Einstein segment. If a description includes

unethical or biased language, an error message appears telling you to change your description.

To help reduce the possibility of creating bias in segments created by generative AI, all demographic

attributes that can create bias are deselected by default. If you encounter something unethical, contact

your Salesforce representative.

1551

Data 360

Einstein Segments in Data 360

Set Up Your Data for Einstein Segments in Data 360

To get proper results when creating an Einstein segment, make sure that your data is prepared

correctly.

Enable Einstein Segments in Data 360

Before you can create Einstein segments, enable generative AI and then turn on Einstein segments.

Create an Einstein Segment in Data 360

Describe your segment to get suggested related attributes that are based on the data found in your

org. To avoid bias and inaccuracies, all demographic attributes are removed. Attributes that produce

fewer than 10 results for the segment population are also removed to improve the segment's accuracy.

How to Write a Good Prompt for Einstein Segments in Data 360

When creating a segment, use certain formats and language to get the best results possible. Provide

descriptive names for data model objects (DMOs) and attributes to ensure that generative AI can

understand them. OpenAI was trained on data that leans toward the United States, which influences

Einstein’s responses. If you require a specific country, enter the name of the country in the prompt.

Improve Your Einstein Segment Creation Results in Data 360

What happens if you receive unclear results, or if the results aren’t necessarily what you’re hoping for?

Use these suggestions to gain more accurate results.

6. 6.  In the Einstein Segment Creation chat, enter a segment description of at least two words using simple

phrases, and then press Enter. After you enter a description, all the words are translated for you into

attributes and values based on the data that exists in your org. A segment description is created based

on the phrase that you entered (1), and the attributes related to the description are created. For

example, Einstein generative AI translates “physical and mental well-being” into different values using

the Primary Hobby attribute. Attributes are divided into suggested attributes (2) and additional
attributes (3). The suggested attributes are the most relevant to your description and are selected by

default. The additional attributes aren’t necessarily relevant to your description. You can deselect any

of the suggested attributes and select any of the additional attributes.

How to Write a Good Prompt for Einstein Segments in Data 360

When creating a segment, use certain formats and language to get the best results possible. Provide

descriptive names for data model objects (DMOs) and attributes to ensure that generative AI can

understand them. OpenAI was trained on data that leans toward the United States, which influences

Einstein’s responses. If you require a specific country, enter the name of the country in the prompt.

Improve Your Einstein Segment Creation Results in Data 360

What happens if you receive unclear results, or if the results aren’t necessarily what you’re hoping for?

Use these suggestions to gain more accurate results.

Refine your metadata with Metadata Studio

Einstein Segment Creation results are optimized with Einstein Data Prism. To get the best results with

Data Prism, use the Metadata Studio to review the generated descriptions for objects and fields, enter

missing information, and remove obsolete objects from the data source. See Metadata Studio.

Make your prompt specific to your brand

Include terms that you use to describe your brand that might not be common for others outside of your
company. For example, if you use a specific customer type, specify this in your prompt, such as “all

members who are customer type= NSH”. If you want to include a specific product or website,

specify this in your prompt, for example, “customers who engaged with website=

“mywesite.com.”

Billing Considerations for Segmentation

Check whether your prompt is ignoring specific fields

If specific fields are being ignored, try using more brand-specific terms or prepositions to simplify the

prompt.

Remove unwanted attributes

If your results contain attributes that you don’t need or want, deselect them so that they aren’t included

with your segment.

Use descriptive terms

If you need specific information, use descriptive terms in your prompt. For example, if you want data

about active users, specify this in your prompt: “active users who engaged today.”

Broaden your search to increase your population count

If you receive a message that your result will produce a small population, try to broaden your search and

focus on the data that you know exists.

Reduce Segmentation Costs

You can lower credit consumption rates for segmentation in several ways.

•  Before publishing a segment, ensure quality of results by previewing them on a sample data set.
•  Run quality checks on your segments by verifying segment membership before publishing.
•  Nest common filters in multiple segments in last membership mode for reuse and lower costs.

Update these settings on segments to minimize consumption.

•  Run Mode--If your use case allows for it, don’t schedule segment publishes. For example, you can
reduce costs when you’re testing and refining a segment by running it only when you’re ready.
•  Frequency, Run Every, and Start Date--Reduce credit consumption by reducing the frequency of

scheduled publishes.

•  Ends--Limit the time period during which the segment runs by setting it to stop running.
•  Lookback Window--Reduce the number of records processed by refining your lookback window to

only the necessary amount of time required by your use case.

Activation and Activation Targets

Activation is the process that publishes a segment to your activation platforms, allowing you to take

action on that data. An activation target is used to store authentication and authorization information

for a given activation platform, like Marketing Cloud Engagement or Meta.

Clean Rooms

Use a clean room to collaborate securely on audience data with other parties without exposing raw

data or compromising confidentiality. Providers can use their data to help companies find appropriate

audiences for their products and services. Consumers can use the insights to refine their targeting

strategies. Use case templates enforce rules around input data, supported queries, and privacy

regulations.

Data Shares

Data Shares provide easy access for external systems to use data in Data 360. With access to data lake

objects (DLOs), data model objects (DMOs), and calculated insight objects (CIOs), you can build

powerful analytical insights and machine learning models. Zero copy data sharing with data shares lets

you share Data 360 objects without loading the data into an external system and gives you near real-

time access to data.

Data Actions in Data 360

Monitor data changes in data model objects and calculated insight objects in Data 360, and send the

change data events to the Salesforce Platform Event, Marketing Cloud Engagement, or a Webhook.

enrichments. Create related list and copy field enrichments for your record pages with data from Data

360.

Activation and Activation Targets

Activation and Activation Targets

Activation is the process that publishes a segment to your activation platforms, allowing you to take

action on that data. An activation target is used to store authentication and authorization information for

a given activation platform, like Marketing Cloud Engagement or Meta.

Once you have created a target, you can publish your segments with contact points and additional

attributes to that activation target. This enables you to power personalized marketing campaigns, create

effective ad campaigns, and deliver consistent customer experiences.

Activation Targets in Data 360

Depending on your use case, data can be activated to various targets, from file storage, external

activation, or to other data model objects (DMOs) in Data 360. Once you know where you want to act

on the segmented data from Data 360, create activation targets for each platform.

Activation for Data 360 Segments

Activation is the process that publishes a segment to activation platforms in Data 360. Before you

activate your segments, it's important to review some activation concepts.

Activation for Data 360 Data Model Objects

Use data from various sources to build complete customer profiles by activating a data model object

(DMO). This feature presents data in a readily actionable format and facilitates personalized customer

experiences. Data 360 offers two methods for DMO activation: streaming and batch, with each

designed for different use cases and destinations.

Activation Templates for Segment-Triggered Flow Setup

Define and save reusable contact point selection logic, including channel selection, source priority

configuration, and contact point filters by using activation templates. Flows use this logic to select the

correct contact points consistently when contacting individuals.

Create an API Activation in Data 360 (Beta)

API activation expands where and how you can initiate activations. API activation gives you the

flexibility to trigger a Data 360 activation from Flow by using an API call.

Advertise with Data 360

Use Data 360 to implement advertising strategies using first-party data. With Data 360, you can

establish a reliable source of truth, seamlessly connect with external platforms, activate audience

segments, and transform them into personalized experiences across all channels.

Capping Communications for B2C Engagements

Set caps on communications with B2C customers, leads, or prospects to ensure compliance with

regulatory requirements, enhance the customer experience, and avoid message fatigue. Optimize your

campaign spend budgets across lines of business by applying department-level thresholds. Stay

compliant with regulatory requirements by avoiding unsolicited, unregulated communications to

targeted entities.

Activation Refresh Types

When creating an activation, choose from two refresh types: full or incremental. A full refresh updates

all records in the segment during activation. An incremental refresh publishes only the added,

updated, and deleted records since the last successful refresh.

Ensuring Integrity in Marketing Cloud Engagement Activation

When multiple Marketing Cloud Engagement (MCE) orgs (EIDs) are involved in an Activation,

unintended data mixing can occur. This happens when subscriber keys from different EIDs are brought

into the same data space and are later activated to a specific EID, which can cause data integrity

issues.

See Also

Salesforce Help: Create a Marketing Cloud Engagement Activation for a Segment

Ensuring Integrity in Marketing Cloud Engagement Activation

When multiple Marketing Cloud Engagement (MCE) orgs (EIDs) are involved in an Activation,

unintended data mixing can occur. This happens when subscriber keys from different EIDs are brought

into the same data space and are later activated to a specific EID, which can cause data integrity issues.

Why is data mixing a concern?

•  A subscriber key isn’t necessarily unique across different EIDs. This means the same key (for example,

SK1) could belong to completely different individuals in separate EIDs.

•  Activating subscriber keys from multiple EIDs together risks sending messages to the wrong

individuals. For example, consider a company that runs two brands under separate EIDs, Tech Gadgets

(EID 1) and Home Essentials (EID 2). If subscriber data from both EIDs is included in an Activation by

mistake, a Tech Gadgets customer might receive a Home Essentials promotion, even if they never

interacted with that brand. Worse, if they had opted out of Home Essentials, this could lead to

compliance violations.

•  Organizations must ensure that user consent is honored and data remains separate to maintain

compliance. The same individual can give consent for different communication channels across EIDs.

For example, they could have given consent for email in EID3 but for WhatsApp in EID4. Keeping data

siloed prevents unintended cross-use of consent preferences across different EIDs.

Example Imagine an organization using three Marketing Cloud connections (EID) and different

business units (BU) to manage subscriber data. Each EID has a unique set of subscriber keys (SK).

•  EID1 covers BU1, BU2, BU3 (with SK1 to SK15)

-
BU1 covers SK1 to SK5
-
BU2 covers SK6 to SK10
-
BU3 covers SK11 to SK15

•  EID2 covers BU4, BU5, BU6 (with SK16 to SK30)

1566

Data 360

Activation and Activation Targets

-
BU4 covers SK16 to SK20
-
BU5 covers SK21 to SK25
-
BU6 covers SK26 to SK30

•  EID3 covers BU7, BU8, BU9 (with SK31 to SK45)

-
BU7 covers SK31 to SK35
-
BU8 covers SK36 to SK40
-
BU9 covers SK41 to SK45

To keep things organized, subscriber data is grouped into data spaces (DS):

•  DS1 contains only data from EID1 (BU1, BU2, BU3).
•  DS2 contains only data from EID2 (BU4, BU5, BU6).
•  DS3 contains only data from EID3 (BU7, BU8, BU9).
•  DS-Global includes all EIDs (BU1–BU9).
•  DS5 contains data from EID1 (BU2, BU3) and EID2 (BU4, BU5).

Activation Scenarios Scenario 1: Activation using DS1 If you create an activation target with DS1,

you’re working only with data from EID1 (BU1, BU2, and BU3).

•  This means only subscriber keys from SK1 to SK15 are activated in the Marketing Cloud

Engagement target (MC1).

•  Data mixing is prevented. Since DS1 contains only EID1 data, there’s no chance of mixing data

from EID2 or EID3.

Scenario 2: Activation using DS-Global DS-Global contains data from all EIDs, but if you’re activating

only BU1 (which belongs to EID1):

•  The system ensures that only SK1 to SK15 (EID1) are activated, even though DS-Global contains
data from EID2 and EID3. If Allow Profile Business Unit Mapping Data (BU-aware) is turned on,

only the SKs for BU1 are activated.

•  Data mixing is prevented because SK16 to SK45 from EID2 and EID3 are automatically blocked

from activation.

Scenario 3: Activation using DS5 DS5 is a mix of EID1 (BU2, BU3) and EID2 (BU4, BU5), and you

want to activate data for BU4.

•  Since BU4 belongs to EID2, only SK16 to SK30 (EID2) are activated in MC2. If Allow Profile
Business Unit Mapping Data (BU-aware) is turned on, only SK16 to SK20 are activated.

•  Data mixing is prevented because SK1 to SK15 (from EID1) are blocked, ensuring data integrity.

Create a Data 360 Activation Target

Create an activation target in Data 360 to publish segments and batch data model objects (DMO) to the

Audience DMO. You can access data from segments and DMOs without a direct connection to an

internal or external target system by publishing the data to the Audience DMO.

You can then retrieve the data using Query APIs, similar to querying any other DMO. Alternatively you

can create an activation-triggered flow to connect to an external API based destination using MuleSoft

connectors in Flow or External Services (HTTP Callouts), where the flow reads the activated data from

Audience DMO and pushes it to the connectors/APIs configured in activation-triggered flow. For more

information, see Create an Activation-Triggered Flow and to find the supported actions for MuleSoft

connectors, see Third-Party Connectors.

•  As an admin, configure connection to your file storage target in Data 360. See, Data Target

Configuration in Data 360.

•  S3 Credentials: If using Amazon S3, have your Access Key and Secret Key ready. Ensure the S3
credentials have these permissions: PutObject, GetObject, ListBucket, DeleteObject, and

GetBucketLocation.

•  S3 Encryption: It is recommended to enable Server-Side Encryption (SSE-S3). Learn more about

1570

Data 360

enabling SSE-S3 encryption.

•  SFTP, GCS, Microsoft Azure: Provide Rename permission in the target system for the activated files

and Modify/Write permission for the folder or directory where the activated files reside.

Available in: All Editions supported by Data 360. See Data 360 edition availability.

USER PERMISSIONS NEEDED

To create an activation target

One of these permission sets:

•  Data Cloud Architect
•  Data Cloud Activation Manager

1. 1.  Go to the Activation Targets tab and click New.

2. 2.  In File Storage, choose your activation platform, and click Next.

3. 3.  Enter a unique name and an optional description.

4. 4.  Configure your activation target platform-specific settings:

• •  Amazon S3

• •  Enter the S3 bucket and folder details.
• •  Provide the S3 Access Key and Secret Key.

Note: To update or delete these keys later, you must delete and recreate the activation target.

• •  Select the target file format.
• •  Select the data space you want to associate your activation target with and click Save.

• •  SFTP, GCS, and Microsoft Azure Blob Storage

• •  Select the connector, the data space, and click Next.
• •  Parent Directory: Inherited from the target connection setup. It is mandatory to have a non-root

parent directory. For more information, see Data Target Configuration in Data 360.

• •  Child Directory: The child directory you provide must already exist in the target location. The child

directory name is case-sensitive. Data 360 will not create one if it doesn’t exist already.
• •  Create a folder within child directory: If selected, activated files are added to a separate folder
-
named <SegmentName_ActivationName>, else they remain in the child directory. The system

automatically replaces folder names containing any character (except alphanumeric and
underscore) with a hyphen (-). Folder names are limited to 200 characters if

<SegmentName_ActivationName> exceeds 200 characters, with any additional characters

automatically truncated.

• •  File Format: Select the activated file format and delimiter for CSV files.
• •  Compression Format: Select the compression format for the activated file. PGP encryption is

supported only for CSV and JSON, but not Parquet.

• •  File Name Type: Choose Predetermined or Custom file name. For predetermined file names, any
character (except alphanumeric and underscore) in SegmentName and ActivationName is

replaced with a hyphen (-).

• •  Data/Time Suffix: Select the file name suffix format, it represents the segment refresh timestamp

in UTC format. The timestamp ranges from a specific date to milliseconds of the day.

• •  Limit type: Activated data is automatically split into multiple files when configured limits are

1571

Data 360

Activation and Activation Targets

reached, such as maximum records per file (default: 100,000) or maximum file size (default: 500

MB).

For example,
• •  For an activation payload with 450,000 records and a 100,000 record limit, the payload is split
-
into multiple files to ensure no single file exceeds 100,000 records.
• •  For an activation payload totalling 3 GB and a 500 MB limit, the payload is split into multiple
-
files to ensure no single file exceeds the 500 MB size limit.

Note File splitting is non-deterministic, and the final number and size of output files may

vary between runs based on data characteristics, file format, compression, encryption, and

processing behavior.

5. 5.  Click Save.

Your activation target is created and these items are added to your file storage activation platform when

the segment is activated:

•  Data files that contain the segment members with additional attributes.

-
For Amazon S3 target, your data files are stored in a subfolder named  Salesforce-
c360-Segments  which is automatically created when the first segment is activated.

•  A segment metadata JSON file in the same directory as your activated data files.

-
For Amazon S3 target, this metadata JSON file serves as a confirmation that the write operation to
your destination is complete and the data is ready for consumption.
-
For SFTP, GCS, and Azure targets, the metadata file and the activated data files may arrive in any
sequence. Hence, the presence of the metadata file doesn’t indicate that activation is complete.

The segment metadata JSON file includes:
-
Segment ID and name
-
Data space ID and name
-
Record count
-
Refresh ID and publish refresh type
-
Attribute names and their corresponding data types

Note For the activated files that are generated in CSV format, the field values follow standard

quoting rules where they are enclosed in double quotes:

•  If a field contains a comma or a new line character, the entire value is quoted. For example:

value1,value2 → "value1,value2".

•  If a field contains double quotes, each quote is escaped with a backslash (\). For example:

"value1","value2" → "\"value1\",\"value2\""

Requirements for External Activation Targets

Requirements for External Activation Targets

Consider these requirements when creating an activation target to an external platform account in Data

360.

Meta (Facebook) Requirements

•  The Ad account must be associated with a Meta Business Manager account.
•  A user must first accept Meta’s Custom Audience Terms of Service for the Business Manager account
that owns or manages the Ad account. For information on Meta’s Terms of Service and how they’re

applied, see the Meta Marketing API Documentation.

•  You can create a Meta activation target only if you’re the owner of the ad account connected to Meta
Business Manager, or the owner has provided you with either admin or advertiser permissions. If your

account is new or if you’ve recently linked to an existing account, it can take a few weeks before you’re

able to create or share a customer list custom audience. If your new account is part of a tenured

business account, you might be able to go through business verification. For more information, see

Meta Business Help Center.

Google Requirements

•  To use Google Customer Match, your account must be in compliance and have a good payment

history.

Google Ads Considerations

•  Certain Customer Match features are available within a Google Ads account depending on the history
and lifetime spend of that account. You can find more information on feature availability in Google's

Advertising Policies Help Documentation.

•  Some categories of products or services are deemed "sensitive" by Google, and consequently,

Customer Match isn’t available for Ad Accounts within those categories. Comprehensive information
about what Google considers a sensitive interest category under Personalized ads and Customer

match policies can be found on the Google website, under the Personalized advertising policies article.

•  Features available to advertisers depend on which requirements your account satisfies.

Amazon Consent Considerations

•  For Amazon Marketing Cloud (AMC) and Amazon DSP, include the Country Code attribute in the

activation target. If the Country Code doesn’t include a selected attribute, it defaults to Unknown and

decreases match rates. You can find more information in Amazon's Help Documentation.

Activation for Data 360 Segments

Activation is the process that publishes a segment to activation platforms in Data 360. Before you

activate your segments, it's important to review some activation concepts.

Activation Membership

Activation membership is the grouping of fields from different data model objects (DMOs) to include in

an activation. If you are using identity resolution ruleset to unify your data, you must use the Unified

Individual data model object (DMO) as the activation membership.

SeeUnified Individual for Activation Membership.

Activations

Reuse filters or other selections across different segments by copying an existing activation. Be aware if

you create a new option by copying an existing activation, the target and the activation membership

can't be changed.

Contact Points

Contact points are a field or set of fields that represent data points that can be used to contact or engage

an individual, for example, email or phone. Contact point selection determines which objects and fields

are included in an activation and sent to an activation target. You can also manage consent by applying

consent-related filters to contact points.

Review more details on Contact Points and Source Priority Order.

Add Related Attributes

Send more personalized communications by adding custom filters and attributes to the activation. When

activating, select the attibutes you want to inlude in the data sent to your activation target.

Learn how to Add Related Attributes to an Activation.

1575

Data 360

Activation and Activation Targets

Activation Refresh Types

When creating an activation, choose from two refresh types: full or incremental. A full refresh updates all

records in the segment during activation. An incremental refresh publishes only the added, updated, and

deleted records since the last successful refresh.

Learn more on the Activation Refresh Type page.

Data Privacy Types

Understand the data privacy types in activation to follow the California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA) law that

gives consumers the right to restrict sharing their data with or selling it to third parties. The privacy types

are CPRA Third-Party and CPRA Service Provider and Not Applicable. These can be established when

setting up an external activation platform in Data Cloud Setup.

Visit California Privacy Protection Agency to learn more about each privacy type.

Activation in Data Cloud One

Data Cloud One is a platform feature that enables multi org enterprises across brands, business units, or

geographic regions to access Data 360 core functions in every org. All orgs are synced from a single Data

360 instance provisioned in the home org. Activation definitions created in the home org are viewable

from every connected companion org in the ecosystem of an enterprise.

Visit Data Cloud One to learn more about Data Cloud One and companion orgs.

Add Related Attributes to an Activation

Send more personalized communications by applying related attributes and filters. You can send

related attributes to Marketing Cloud Engagement, Data Cloud, and cloud file storage platforms such

as Amazon S3, SFTP, Microsoft Azure Blob Storage, and Google Cloud Storage (GCS).

Contact Points and Source Priority Order

1576

Data 360

Activation and Activation Targets

Contact point selection determines which objects and fields are included in an activation and sent to

an activation target. Use the source priority order to determine which contact point value is selected

for the activation.

Add Filters to Contact Points in Activation

When activating a Data 360 segment, you can filter and sort contact points to ensure you are targeting

the right audience on the right channel with the right permissions. This feature is essential for

managing customer consent, preventing duplicate messages, and improving the personalization of

your campaigns.

Add Filters to the Activation Membership

Data 360 activation membership filters allows you to send more personalized communications by

adding custom filters to the activation membership. Add filters to ensure that only the intended

audiences are being targeted.

Activating Subsegments in a Data 360 Waterfall Segment

You can activate an individual subsegment in a waterfall segment or all subsegments at one time.

Including all subsegments in a waterfall segment in a single data extension eliminates the need for

multiple activations and additional post-activation stitching. When you activate the data extension, all

the users are entered into the journey but directed down different paths based on their subsegments.

It improves marketing campaign effectiveness and efficiency. After creating a waterfall segment,

activate the segment to the Marketing Cloud Engagement activation target or any file storage target.

Calculated Insights in Activation

Use Data 360 Calculated Insights to enable activation journey decisions and message personalization.

Segmentation Filters vs. Activation Filters

Segmentation and activation use different filters for different purposes. Apply filters to a segment to

narrow your audience. Use activation filters to narrow down relevant values with related attributes that

personalize messages.

Set Output Name for Activation Attributes

When you configure an activation in Data 360, you can customize the attribute names in your output

file or stream. Custom attribute names help match the naming conventions required by your

activation target. Use the output namefield ( preferred name) to define these values.

Unified Individual for Activation Membership

To take advantage of identity resolution, use the Unified Individual data model object (DMO) as the
Activation Membership. With identity resolution, you combine data from disparate data sources to

create one Unified Individual. When selecting Unified Individual as the DMO, the Individual ID

attribute is included and not the Unified Individual ID.

View Activations in Data Explorer

View your activation data for a specific activation target in Data Cloud. You can view results up to the

past 30 days.

Audience Data Model Object

Understand and analyze your activated audience over time using audience data model objects
(DMOs). There are two types of related DMOs, audience and audience latest DMOs.

Streaming Audit Data Model Object

Use the streaming audit data model object (DMO) to track and audit the data sent from your real-time
streaming activations.

Your segment publishes on the next publish scheduled for the selected activation target. When the

segment publishes for the first time, and if the activation count is greater than zero, a data extension is

created in Marketing Cloud Engagement, and the segment records are added to it. To check if your

• •  Calculated Insights—Add your Calculated Insights metrics to the activation, and apply dimension

filters for more granular insights.

a. a.  Drag additional attributes to the canvas. If you select different columns with similar information, all

the unique combinations are added to the output.

To provide a unique attribute name in the output file, click the edit icon.

When activating additional attributes, primary or foreign key fields aren’t available as an option

because they aren’t exposed for activation. To see primary or foreign key fields during activation,

create a formula field that copies those fields. The formula field is included as an additional

attribute for activation. In the lakehouse, number data type fields are stored as decimals, not

integers. Therefore in activation, the fields appear as decimals, except for primary keys.

b. b.  Save your changes.

attribute that's included automatically based on the Activation Membership object chosen during

activation creation.

• •  Use the column headers to identify and match the corresponding column data at the destination. If

an activation is run multiple times, the order of attributes or columns in the activated file is

ensure its future runs have consistent order of attributes or columns.

Ingest and Model Digital Identifiers for JSON-based External Activation Targets

Ingest and model your digital identifier data by using the standard  ContactPointDigitalId  data

model object (DMO). Independent Software Vendors (ISV) use the activation toolkit to build activations

that query this DMO to resolve digital identities across digital media platforms.

REQUIRED EDITIONS
REQUIRED EDITIONS

Available in: Lightning Experience

Available in: Developer, Enterprise and Unlimited

Editions

Note To activate anonymous digital identifiers, it's recommended to use ContactPointDigitalID

DMO instead of mapping the digital identifiers to custom fields on the Individual DMO.

Before mapping your data, it’s important to understand the target blueprint. Map your source identifiers
to the  ContactPointDigitalId  DMO. For activations to work, this DMO must have an established

Many-to-One (N:1) relationship to the Individual DMO (linking
ContactPointDigitalId.ssot__IndividualId__c  to  Individual.ssot__Id__c ). You can

verify or create this relationship in the Data Model tab. This mapping is mandatory when you use the

activation toolkit for JSON-based external activation platforms that rely on specific digital identifiers (for

example, UID2, RampID).

Note If your activation only targets email or phone-based destinations (by using
ContactPointEmail  or  ContactPointPhone ), this DMO is optional, though it’s recommended

to centralize all digital identities here.

Prepare Your Source Data

You can ingest data via multiple methods, including CSV/File ingestion, Ingestion API, or WebSDK.

Regardless of the ingestion method (batch or streaming), your source data structure must support the

granular mapping required by the DMO. Pivot your source data so that you have one column for the

identifier's type and another for its value.

Note The 'Digital ID Type' and 'Digital ID Value' are specific fields on the ContactPointDigitalId DMO.

Your source data must be explicitly mapped and ingested into these fields.

Configure the ID Type Mapping

Before you begin mapping your data stream, make sure that the identifier types in your source data

perfectly match the configuration in the Data 360 Setup page.

As a Data 360 Admin user, go to Data 360 Setup > External Activation Target > [Target Name] > ID

Type Mapping and configure the ID type mapping.

The exact string value in your source data's Digital_ID_Type column (for example, "TD ID") must perfectly

match the string configured in the ID Type column by the Data 360 administrator. Because Data 360 uses

this string as a strict filter during activation, a case-sensitive mismatch (for example, a value in your data

might appear as “TDID,” whereas the Data 360 setup lists it as “TD ID”) results in zero activated records.

Create and Map Your Data Stream

After preparing your source file, create your data stream and map it to the standard DMOs.

Note Data 360 doesn’t automatically link new DMOs. After you complete these mapping steps,
you’ll likely need to create the relationship manually between  ContactPointDigitalId  and

Individual .

1. 1.  Create a data stream and point it to your data source.

2. 2.  In the mapping canvas, map your profile data to the Individual DMO.

• •  Map Individual_ID -> Individual.IndividualId
• •  Map FirstName -> Individual.FirstName
• •  If you're activating anonymous users, you don't have standard profile data like a First Name or a

known Customer ID. In this case, you must use a persistent digital identifier (such as a Device ID or
Cookie ID) to act as the individual's profile ID. Map this value to the  ssot__IndividualId__c

field to represent the anonymous individual in the data model.

3. 3.  In the mapping canvas, map your source fields from the data lake object (DLO) to the specific fields on

the ContactPointDigitalId DMO. Correct field-level mapping is critical to prevent zero population errors
during activation.

Considerations for Selecting Related Attributes in Data 360 Activations

Related attributes are data fields that belong to data model objects (DMO) connected to your primary

or activation DMO. These attributes help you access information from other objects that are linked

through a defined relationship path. There’s a direct relationship with the DMO, related attributes, and

1592

Data 360

Activation and Activation Targets

the filters you can apply.

See Also

Salesforce Help: Segment Your Data with Attributes

Considerations for Selecting Related Attributes in Data 360 Activations

Related attributes are data fields that belong to data model objects (DMO) connected to your primary or

activation DMO. These attributes help you access information from other objects that are linked through

a defined relationship path. There’s a direct relationship with the DMO, related attributes, and the filters

you can apply.

Note For engagement data, activation supports a 90-day lookback window. If related attributes are

selected for an activation with a rapid segment publish, the lookback window is seven days.

Activation considers engagement data within this window, and any records outside of this window

aren't considered when selecting your output values. Profiles might be included in the activation if

an engagement date falls within a 24-month window for a segment. Specific engagement records

might not be included in the activation if they fall outside the 90-day lookback window.

When selecting related attributes, consider these guidelines:

•  You can activate up to 25 values per related attribute.
•  You can select up to 300 related attributes per activation.
•  You can use up to 8 DMOs per activation.
•  You can use up to 10,000 activations with related attributes. After reaching that limit, you can choose
to delete related attributes from existing activations, delete unused activations, or create activations

with only direct attributes.

•  The segment size is checked at the time of activation. If the segment has more than 150 million

records and contains related attributes when you publish, the segment doesn’t activate.

•  A single customer (or Individual) can have multiple Sales Orders, each tied to different order details.
You can select attributes from different DMOs across multiple paths from your activation DMO. For

example:
-
Individual → Engagement (email, website)
-
Individual → Sales Order → Order Details

•  When applying filters on DMOs, you can use attributes from the filtered DMO itself or any of its related
child DMOs. Attributes from unselected or inactive DMOs can also be used for filtering. Filters are

optional. If no filter is applied, the activation considers all data from the selected DMO.

•  The segmentation and activation attribute libraries achieve different purposes so they behave

differently. In segmentation, the entire DMO hierarchy is displayed. In activation, the DMOs that are

one hop away from the object are displayed. To get to other DMOs, click through the hierarchy.
•  Activation doesn’t automatically acquire segmentation filters. To activate specific values for your
attribute, apply filters to your activation. Use segmentation filters to find users who qualify for the

segment. Use activation filters to find attributes for message personalization.

1593

Data 360

Activation and Activation Targets

Related Attributes Filtering

Related Attributes filtering allows users to include only relevant data in the activation payload, by

applying specific filter conditions. This makes sure that the activated data aligns with the campaign’s

intent.

For example, a marketer wants to send an email to customers about their orders currently in the
Shipping In Progress state. They’ll select attributes like Order ID and Order Details for activation,

and apply a filter where Order Status = "Shipping In Progress". This ensures that only orders

matching this status are included in the output.

•  Filters applied upstream are inherited downstream, ensuring consistent filtering throughout the

activation.

•  A locked or grayed-out filter view in child DMOs indicates inherited filters.
•  DMOs at the same level on different paths don't inherit each other’s filters.

Here's an example:

DMO Name

Attributes Selected

Notes

To retrieve all Sales Order IDs where the order includes the Product Name Toy and has a Product

Summary marked as Good, you need to apply the filters on the Sales Order DMO.

As a result, only those sales order IDs that match the filter criteria are included. The filtering logic flows

downstream from the DMOs where the filters are applied. This means that if you are activating attributes

from Order Details, Product Detail, and Product Summary, they will all inherit the upstream filters

applied on Sales Order. These filters affect the Order Details and Sales Order DMOs.

Filters aren't applied upstream, so any DMO upstream of Sales Order, such as the Individual DMO,

remains unaffected. Consequently, the inherited filter also makes sure that all attributes downstream of
Sales Order are implicitly filtered to show only details related to Toy and summaries marked as Good.

Understanding DMO Counts

•  When related attributes are selected from multiple paths, each data model object involved counts

toward the DMO limit.

•  DMOs used only for filtering also count toward the limit.
•  However, if a DMO is already included for attribute selection, using additional attributes from the

DMO for filters doesn't add to the count. For example, if you select an attribute from Product Details

for activation and also use an attribute from the same DMO for filtering, it still counts as one DMO in

the limit calculation.

Here are some examples of the DMO count:

•  Selecting an attribute from Product Details results in a DMO count of three: Sales Order, Order Details,
and Product Details. If an attribute from Product Summary is then added, it only increments the count

by one, as the initial DMOs aren't recounted.

•  If you activate attributes from Order Details without applying any filters, the path traverses through

Sales Order, resulting in a DMO count of two.

•  If you activate attributes only from Product Details and Product Summary without applying any filters,

the DMO count is four.

Source Priority Order

Use source priority order to determine which contact point value is selected for an activation when

multiple values are available. Also, to reorder which contact point value is selected for segment members

with data from multiple sources. You can change the priority by adding, reordering, or deleting sources.

All contact points remain part of the Unified Individual DMO after unifying your source data in Identity

Resolution. Identity Resolution reconciliation rules only reconcile fields for the unified individual object,

not unified contact point objects. Use source priority to make sure that you deliver a contact point from

your desired data source to your activation target regardless of your reconciliation rules. If the Email Type

didn't select Any, then the Primary Flag must be mapped on the corresponding contact point DMO for

contact points to match.

Add Filters to Contact Points in Activation

the right audience on the right channel with the right permissions. This feature is essential for managing

customer consent, preventing duplicate messages, and improving the personalization of your

campaigns.

REQUIRED EDITIONS

send a marketing campaign to their primary personal email, and only if they have given you consent to

do so.

Activating Subsegments in a Data 360 Waterfall Segment

You can activate an individual subsegment in a waterfall segment or all subsegments at one time.

Including all subsegments in a waterfall segment in a single data extension eliminates the need for

multiple activations and additional post-activation stitching. When you activate the data extension, all

the users are entered into the journey but directed down different paths based on their subsegments. It

improves marketing campaign effectiveness and efficiency. After creating a waterfall segment, activate

the segment to the Marketing Cloud Engagement activation target or any file storage target.

When selecting the subsegments within the waterfall segment for activation, you have the option to

select ‘All Segments’ or individual subsegments. The activation outcome depends on your selection.

For example, your waterfall segment contains subsegments A, B, and C. You activate all three segments

to the target by selecting All Segments . Later, when you add subsegments D and E to the waterfall
segment, they’re automatically included for activation in the next publish.

However, if you activate subsegments A, B, and C individually, subsegments that you add later to the

waterfall aren’t included automatically in the next publish. Instead, you must manually select these

subsegments for activation.

Calculated Insights in Activation

Use Data 360 Calculated Insights to enable activation journey decisions and message personalization.

Calculated Insights metrics can help drive content personalization in Marketing Cloud Engagement.

Drag your completed Calculated Insights metrics onto any new or existing activation. Add dimension

filters to your Calculated Insights metric for more granular insights on an activation.

Calculated Insights includes two different categories when creating metrics: aggregatable and non-

aggregatable.

Aggregatable Metrics

Dimension filters are optional for aggregatable metrics and you can still aggregate on the insight.

Non-Aggregatable Metrics

At least one dimension filter is required for non-aggregatable metrics in order to narrow down the

attribute to one specific value.

•  Text
•  Numeric

Example If the ‘Purchase Rank’ measure = 1, the ‘Product’ dimension = Pizza, and the ‘Date’

dimension = January, you can find one specific value since you added dimensions to the attribute. If

you just had the ‘Purchase Rank’ measure, that itself is non-aggregatable and there would be no

value.

Note If a dimension filter is a Date or DateTime for non-aggregatable metrics, the insight appears

but the non-aggregatable metric is hidden. All aggregate metrics are available to be added as

attributes still.

Segmentation Filters vs. Activation Filters

Segmentation and activation use different filters for different purposes. Apply filters to a segment to

narrow your audience. Use activation filters to narrow down relevant values with related attributes that

personalize messages.

For example, as an online retailer, you want to run an email campaign targeting your customers that have

purchased video games in the past 2 months. You want to personalize the message by including the

product name of the video game that the customer most recently purchased.

Begin the process in segmentation by applying filter criteria to narrow your audience to customers who

have purchased video games in the past 2 months.

In activation, add the Product Name related attribute to include the product names of the items that the

customers have purchased. However, during the past 2 months, customers could have made other

purchases in addition to video games. To include only video game purchases in the email, apply a filter

to the attribute, such as Product Category is equal to Video Games. If you don’t apply a filter to the

attribute, other products that the customer has purchased are included in the email.

See Also

Salesforce Help: Segmentation Filter Examples

Set Output Name for Activation Attributes

When you configure an activation in Data 360, you can customize the attribute names in your output file

or stream. Custom attribute names help match the naming conventions required by your activation

target. Use the output namefield ( preferred name) to define these values.

By default, the Output Name field shows the API name of the attribute with system prefixes and suffixes

removed. To override the default API name, enter a custom preferred value in the Output Name field.

Data 360 uses this value as the column header or field name in the activation output.

The output names must be unique across all attributes in the activation, including attributes from

different data model objects (DMOs). Output names can contain only alphanumeric characters.

See Also

Salesforce Help: Create Activation for a Segment

Unified Individual for Activation Membership

To take advantage of identity resolution, use the Unified Individual data model object (DMO) as the

Activation Membership. With identity resolution, you combine data from disparate data sources to

create one Unified Individual. When selecting Unified Individual as the DMO, the Individual ID attribute

is included and not the Unified Individual ID.

Contact Points for a Unified Individual

If you have data from multiple data sources in Data 360, use Unified Individual as the Activation

Membership. Selecting Individual instead of Unified Individual as the Activation Membership can result

in duplicate entries in your count. When any DMO besides Unified Individual is selected as the Activation

Membership, Data 360 includes all contact points associated with the object.

Data 360 activates one row for a Unified Individual. Unified Individual includes different fields

depending on which contact point channel you select.

Audience Data Model Object

Understand and analyze your activated audience over time using audience data model objects (DMOs).

There are two types of related DMOs, audience and audience latest DMOs.

1616

Data 360

Activation and Activation Targets

An Audience DMO show when profiles are added, updated, deleted, or unchanged. View profile details,

such as the activated attributes, when the activation occurred, and which segment it belongs to.

An Audience Latest DMO lets you quickly find and retrieve information on the most recent activation

publish from Data Explorer or through the API. You can query the latest activation payload using only the

activation ID, without needing to filter by the last published timestamp for history-based queries.

However, these DMOs don't include the delete delta type, which is only available in and audience DMO.

When you create or edit an activation, an Audience DMO is created for each activation target in

Marketing Cloud Engagement, Amazon S3, SFTP, Google Cloud Storage (GCS), Microsoft Azure Blob

Storage, Marketing Cloud Personalization, Data Cloud, and B2C Commerce.

For example, if you create five Engagement activation targets, ten audience DMOs are created. Five

historical audience DMOs and five audience latest DMOs. When you delete the connected activation

target or the DMO, the audience DMO is deleted. You can’t delete the Audience DMO if an activation is

using it. The first time you save an activation for each activation target, it takes longer than usual because

the Audience DMO is being created.

Streaming Audit Data Model Object

Use the streaming audit data model object (DMO) to track and audit the data sent from your real-time

streaming activations.

REQUIRED EDITIONS
REQUIRED EDITIONS

Available in:

Unlike standard audience DMOs, the streaming audit DMO is a single, append-only object. It serves as a

continuous historical log of everything sent via a streaming DMO activation. Use it to view the exact data

payload, precise commit and processing timestamps, and metadata about the streaming job itself.

An audit DMO is automatically created when you configure a streaming activation for the first time for an

activation target. For example, if you create a streaming DMO activation, a corresponding streaming

Audit DMO is created to log all its activity. The lifecycle of the DMO is tied to its activation target. You

can't manually delete the DMO while the activation target exists, regardless of whether it has active

activations or not. The audit DMO is deleted only when the activation target is deleted.

Activate Segments on Households

Activate segments built on the Household object in Data Cloud to target individuals within those

households.

When you create a segment that identifies specific households, you can use activation to send marketing

campaigns to them. Since a household itself doesn't have a contact point like an email address, the

activation process targets individuals within the household.

After you select a segment built on the Household object, you can choose how to target its members

using Activation Membership. This is the activate-on entity.

Activate on Household: Target One Individual or Unified Individual Per
Household

For each household in your segment, Data Cloud selects the single best individual or unified individual to

target. Data Cloud uses your configured source priority and contact point filtering rules to determine the

individual or unified individual and contact point (for example, the most reliable email address) to

represent the household. This is useful for campaigns where you only need to reach each home once,

1622

Data 360

Activation and Activation Targets

such as catalogs, or a single promotional email addressed to the household.

Activate on Unified Individual or Individual: Target All Household Members

For each household in your segment, Data Cloud targets every individual (or unified individual)

associated with that household. The activation sends a record for each person in the household to the

destination target. This option is useful for campaigns where the message is relevant to each person,

such as offers for a family mobile plan, announcements for a local event, or information about a new

streaming service.

Refine Your Audience with Activation Membership Filtering

There might be certain members of the household that don't wish to receive the campaign message. For

example, you might want to send a special offer only to the individuals in a household who don't yet use

a certain service or product. You can achieve this with Activation Membership Filtering.

This feature is useful when your Segment On entity (Household) is different from your Activate On entity

(Individual or Unified Individual). It allows you to apply a second layer of filtering to the members of the

households your segment has already selected.

For example, your campaign goal is to send a promotional offer to all households with at least one

member that has an annual pass, but only send an offer to the individuals in the household that don’t

have an annual pass.

Your segment can identify households with at least one Annual Pass Holder. To send a promotional offer

to the non-subscribers in those homes, first choose to activate on Individual or Unified Individual to

target all household members. Then use Activation Membership Filtering to target individuals in the

household that do not have the Annual Pass, like Annual Pass Holder is equal to 'No'. This action

precisely targets only the desired members of the household.

Streaming DMO Activation

Streaming activation is designed for near real-time use cases and sends data to a destination as events

occur.

Standard and Custom Events

When creating a streaming activation, you can use either a standard or a custom event.

•  Standard Events—These are predefined by the destination platform (for example, Meta CAPI). All

necessary attributes and values are included automatically. This is the recommended approach for

first-time users.

•  Custom Events—Create custom events and add only the attributes you want to provide a more tailored

activation experience.

Note You can’t copy an existing DMO activation. However, you can edit and update the end date of

an activation.

Batch DMO Activation

Use batch activation when you need to send a complete dataset for analysis, archiving, or large-scale

marketing campaigns. Common scenarios include:

•  Exporting a full customer profile table to a data warehouse for business intelligence.
•  Sending a large, comprehensive list of product recommendations or personalized attributes to

Marketing Cloud Engagement.

•  Archiving a complete snapshot of a DMO to a secure SFTP location for compliance or record-keeping.

1624

Data 360

Considerations

Activation and Activation Targets

•  You can activate external DMOs if they are accelerated. In Bring Your Own Lake (BYOL) scenarios, only

accelerated DMOs are supported. Non-accelerated external DMOs are not supported.

•  Batch DMO activation supports Profile, Engagement, and Other DMO types. You can’t use it for

Audience DMOs and certain system-generated DMOs.

•  Unlike batch segment activations, there’s currently no option to set a custom schedule for Batch DMO

activations in the UI.

•  When activating an Engagement DMO, the activation payload includes records only from the last 90

days. It doesn’t send the entire history of engagement records.

Activation Templates for Segment-Triggered Flow Setup

Define and save reusable contact point selection logic, including channel selection, source priority

configuration, and contact point filters by using activation templates. Flows use this logic to select the

correct contact points consistently when contacting individuals.

REQUIRED EDITIONS
REQUIRED EDITIONS

Available in: All Editions supported by Data 360. See Data 360 edition availability.

As activations have evolved to include features such as contact point filtering and source priority

ordering, the configuration required to select the right contact points has become more complex. Teams

often reuse the same filtering and priority logic across many campaigns, especially for consent

compliance and contact point selection.

Activation templates solve this problem by letting you save commonly used contact point configurations

one time and then reference them from segment-triggered flows. Instead of configuring contact point

selection logic from scratch in each flow, the flow reads the predefined logic stored in the template.

Note This feature is exclusively supported in Segment-triggered flows.

Benefits of Activation Templates

•  Save time: Define contact point selection logic one time and reuse it across multiple flows.
•  Reduce errors: Apply source priority rules and contact point filters consistently without manual

reconfiguration.

•  Improve compliance: Standardize consent and contact point filter configurations to meet regulatory

requirements, such as GDPR.

•  Enable flows: Give segment-triggered flows access to sophisticated contact point selection logic that

was previously available only in the activation UI.

How Activation Templates Work

An activation template is a nonpublishable configuration that stores contact point selection metadata.

The template itself is never published to a destination and has no publish schedule or activation jobs.

Instead, it serves as a metadata container that holds the logic for contact point selection.

Each template is associated with a specific data space and data model object (DMO), such as Individual

or Unified Individual. The DMO association determines which flows can reference the template.

When a flow references an activation template, the flow engine reads the template's stored logic to

identify the correct contact points for each individual in the segment. This feature provides consistent,

reliable contact point selection without requiring the Flow Builder to re-create complex filtering logic

manually.

1630

Data 360

Activation and Activation Targets

Note Updates to a template after a flow has used it don't retroactively change the results of previous

flow executions.

Template Components

An activation template includes these configurations.

•  Contact point channels: Pre-selected channels such as email, phone (SMS), or WhatsApp.
•  Source priority: The evaluation order for contact point values when multiple values exist for the same
channel. Each row in the source priority table represents a combination of source, source object,

contact point type, and active status.

For example, you can configure the priority so that a primary email from the Marketing Cloud source

with a Lead source object is selected before a primary email from the same source with a Prospect

source object. Rows higher in the table take priority.

•  Contact point filters: Filter criteria applied to contact point DMOs or consent DMOs to make sure that

only compliant, valid contact points are selected.

Example To comply with GDPR consent regulations, a global company operating in Europe needs to

ensure proper compliance when contacting individuals via segment-triggered flows. The marketing

operations manager addresses this by creating an activation template, named "GDPR email

Compliance," which includes:

•  Email as the contact point channel
•  A source priority configuration where a primary email from the Marketing Cloud source with a
Lead source object is first priority, followed by a primary email from Marketing Cloud with a

Prospect source object, and then a business email from S3 as the lowest priority

•  Contact point filters requiring explicit email opt-in consent

When a flow builder creates a segment-triggered flow, it references the "GDPR email Compliance"

template. The flow engine uses the template's stored logic to select the correct, consent-compliant

email address for each individual in the segment based on the defined priority order. The flow

builder doesn't need to process all GDPR consent requirements or manually configure the contact
point selection.

Create a Reusable Template for Contact Point Selection

Create an activation template to define a reusable contact point selection logic that segment-triggered

flows can reference. Templates store channel selections, source priority configuration, and contact

point filters in a single, reusable configuration.

Review Insights

Data 360

attempts to generate insights for all segment activations to Google Ads and Amazon. Insights are added

to audience insight data model objects (DMOs).

Learn more about the Audience Insights Data Model Object.

Amazon Ads and Amazon Marketing Cloud Insights in Activation

Delve into your customers’ unique characteristics, interests, and behaviors with Amazon Marketing

Cloud (AMC) audience insights reporting. When you activate a segment to Amazon Ads AMC, an

audience report is generated. The report provides demographic insights on customers who are actively

researching products and their affinity groups based on lifestyle, long-term buying habits, and

interests.

Google Audience Insights in Activation

Delve into your customers’ unique characteristics, interests, and behaviors with insights from a Google

audience report within Data Cloud. After you activate a segment to Google, an audience report is

generated in 5–7 days. The report provides insights in terms of demographics and customers who are

actively researching products and their affinity groups based on their lifestyle, long-term buying habits,

and interests.

Audience Insights Data Model Object in Data Cloud

The Audience Insights data model object (DMO) provides insights into the audiences that you’ve

activated on Google advertising platforms with the Ad Audiences connector. You can retrieve records

from multiple activated audiences and delve into their similarities and differences. The DMO is

updated every 48 hours and stores audience insights records for the previous 90 days, enabling you to

track the long-term impact of a campaign and how your audiences evolve.

Audience Match Count for Advertising Activations

Match Count is the approximate number of users from your audience segments who have been

successfully matched on an external advertising partner platform (like Facebook, Google Ads, or
TikTok). Monitor the match count of your segment list activations to understand the reach and size of

the audience you are activating.

See Also

Trailhead: Advertising with Data 360

Amazon Ads and Amazon Marketing Cloud Insights in Activation

Delve into your customers’ unique characteristics, interests, and behaviors with Amazon Marketing Cloud

(AMC) audience insights reporting. When you activate a segment to Amazon Ads AMC, an audience

report is generated. The report provides demographic insights on customers who are actively researching

products and their affinity groups based on lifestyle, long-term buying habits, and interests.

1635

Data 360

Report

Activation and Activation Targets

The report generates scores by comparing targeted users within the segment—the Advertiser

Audience—with the broader targeted user population. The scores represent the likelihood of the

Advertiser Audience members being part of a specific demographic or behavioral category.  The breadth

and depth of insights can change based on the unique user impression reach of recent ad campaigns.

The more people who see your ads the more insights you get, and the more statistically significant they

become.

Users must have been exposed to at least 1 ad on Amazon to be included when calculating the

population distributions (which are the inputs to the propensity score).  For example,  If I've served an ad

to 10M unique users in the last 90, then 10M profiles will be available for me to use when running the

report.

Google Audience Insights in Activation

Delve into your customers’ unique characteristics, interests, and behaviors with insights from a Google

audience report within Data Cloud. After you activate a segment to Google, an audience report is

generated in 5–7 days. The report provides insights in terms of demographics and customers who are

actively researching products and their affinity groups based on their lifestyle, long-term buying habits,

and interests.

Report Scores

The report generates scores by comparing the activated segment membership population, known as the

Customer Match audience, with the average Google user population in a particular country. The scores

represent the likelihood of members within the Customer Match audience being part of a specific

demographic or behavioral category.

Demographics categorize the members based on age and gender. The In-Market category shows

customers who are actively researching products, so potentially in the market for specific services or

products. Affinity categorizes customers who exhibit specific characteristics.

For the In-Market and Affinity categories, the report includes up to 20 scores. The insights selected are

based on the top 20 highest scores.

Considerations and Privacy

To qualify for audience insights reporting, the activated segment population must be more than 1,000

users. The report is updated when there’s a major change to the segment membership.

To ensure that insights remain anonymous and can’t be linked back to individuals, Google implements

privacy safeguards. Some of the privacy measures include:

•  Category redaction—In certain cases, high-indexing categories are excluded from a report if the user

1636

Data 360

Activation and Activation Targets

population is considered too small. This exclusion preserves user privacy.

•  Differential privacy—To protect individual membership records without significantly impacting

reporting results, Google employs algorithms that add randomized noise to the reports. As a result,

insights scores are considered approximations and can exhibit slight fluctuations over time.

Match Count is the approximate number of users from your audience segments who have been

successfully matched on an external advertising partner platform (like Facebook, Google Ads, or TikTok).

Monitor the match count of your segment list activations to understand the reach and size of the

audience you are activating.
