Syncing Copy Field Enrichments

Learn how data is copied and synced between Data 360 and your org for copy field enrichments. Get tips

for troubleshooting data syncing and changing enrichments.

The last step in creating a copy field enrichment is to start a data sync. The first sync is always a full sync.

Full Sync And Incremental Sync

Copy field enrichments use two types of sync.

•  Full Sync is a series of bulk jobs that started when you create the enrichment. The bulk jobs copy
records in batches. It can take hours for all of the jobs to be complete. A full sync job can run for a

maximum of 24 hours. It can process 60–100 million records, depending on the environment. Each

job must be completed before the data is fully available. The log for each job is available separately in

the Sync History tab for the enrichment.

•  Incremental Sync uses batched events to keep your field data up to date. Incremental sync is triggered

by any change in Data 360 data for the fields you're copying.

Note If more than 250,000 data changes occur in a transaction after any filter conditions are

applied for copy field enrichment, the incremental sync is replaced by a full sync. A full sync reduces

latency in data syncs for large volumes of changes. After the full sync completes, the system

switches to incremental sync again. To learn about the cost of copy field enrichment for each sync

method, see Considerations for Enrichment Cost Impact.

Stopping and Restarting Syncs

If you stop syncing your enrichment, no more data is copied into your org, but no data or fields are

removed. If you restart your sync, it performs a full sync again and copies all of the data from Data 360,

which can take days. However, Salesforce recommends periodically restarting the sync, because

incremental syncs behave like events and can occasionally have incomplete data for transactions with

over 100,000 changes.

1758

Data 360

Enrich Your Org with 360 Data and Insights

Troubleshooting Sync

The Sync History tab shows every sync that changes a record in your org. It lists the type of sync and

indicates its status. To see the Sync History tab, click the name of an enrichment in the list screen.

For full syncs, the Sync History tab Details column shows links to logs for each batch of changes. The logs

expire after 7 days and are no longer accessible.

In some cases, a sync job succeeds as a whole, but specific records fail to be copied over. To see if

individual records are failing to sync, check the Sync History tab Records Excluded column.

For incremental syncs, any errors that are encountered are shown in the Sync History tab Details column.

If no records are changed in an incremental sync, the sync doesn’t appear in the Sync History tab.

If you have a key qualifier specified and the sync seems to be copying over the wrong data, check to

make sure that the key qualifer is correct. If it’s incorrect, stop the sync, specify the correct key qualifier,

and restart the sync.

Record Exclusions and Errors

Records are excluded from sync for several reasons.

•  Locked data—data locked by another user at the time of sync is excluded from the sync
•  Orphaned data—records that don't have a corresponding user in the org are excluded from the sync.
For example, assume that org A and org B have records ingested into Data 360 and you're syncing

records from org A. Some amount of the records to sync are customers that only exist in org B and

those records are excluded. You only sync records that are relevant for your customers. These records

are orphaned records because they don't have a parent object in your org.

•  Mismatched Data—data that contains characters or other issues that can’t be included in the org. These

records fail validation and can’t be synced.

Deployment Considerations

When deploying copy field enrichments and related metadata, consider these details.

•  If you deploy a copy field enrichment to a target org that already has an enrichment with the same

definition, the deployment succeeds, but no changes are made.

•  To deploy a data model object (DMO), your data kit must include either a data lake object (DLO)
mapping or an associated data stream. To merge back relationships between DMOs or calculated

insight objects (CIOs), ensure that the DMOs or CIOs meet this requirement, and that you add the

Field Source Target Relationship to the outbound change set.

•  Data 360 dependencies: you must manually add data streams or any relevant DLOs. If a CIO is

required for the copy field enrichment, ensure that its dependencies (for example, DMO) are included.

•  CRM dependencies: When adding items to a Change Set, custom CRM fields are automatically

discovered. If needed, you must manually add custom CRM objects to the Change Set.

•  Copy fields are always deployed in an inactive (draft) state. You must manually activate the copy field

enrichments after deploying them.

Limitations

These actions are not supported for copy field enrichments.

•  Deploying an updated copy field enrichment is not supported.
•  Undeploy is not supported.

Enrichment Troubleshooting

Diagnose issues with enrichments and fix them.

Data in the org depends on data space, object, mapping, and data ingestion in Data Cloud.

Blank Related List

If a user complains that a related list is blank, but you can see the data, make sure that they have data

space access control for any permission set assigned to them.

1760

Data 360

Enrich Your Org with 360 Data and Insights

If you see that the related list is blank, make sure that you don’t need a key qualifier for your data stream.

You only need a key qualifier in the rare case that data from your org is ingested via another system or

service and not directly by using the CRM connector.

Data Cloud supports specific date formats. Make sure that you’re using a supported date format.

Blank Copy Field

If no data is available for the field you’re copying, make sure that:

•  You selected a valid ID matching method. If the criteria you’re using doesn’t matchthe underlying data,

then no data is returned.

•  The object and data space configured for it hasn’t changed.
•  The data stream for the objects is connected successfully and ingesting data.
•  You specified the correct key qualifier. You don’t usually require a key qualifier. However, if you
specified the wrong key qualifier, it can cause the wrong data to be copied over for a copy field

enrichment.

Copy Field Is Copying the Wrong Data

If the copy field isn’t showing data from the correct field, make sure that you specified the correct key

qualifier. You only require a key qualifier if you aren’t using the CRM connector to ingest data from your

org into Data Cloud. If you specified the wrong key qualifier, it can cause the wrong data to be copied

over for a copy field enrichment.

If the copy field isn’t showing the data you expect, for example, it shows cases related to personal

purchases, rather than business purchases, make sure you’re using an ID matching method that matches

against the correct object.

Copy Field Full Sync is Failing

Make sure that you set the permissions on the Contact or Lead object for the integration user. See Enrich
Your Org with 360 Data and Insights for instructions on setting the permissions. After you set the

permissions, stop the sync, and then start it again.

Unexpected Behavior

If your enrichment doesn’t behave as expected and you tried the other troubleshooting steps, make sure

that:

•  The object and data space configured for it hasn’t changed.
•  The data stream for the objects is connected successfully and ingesting data.

Automate Flows in Data 360

Automate Flows in Data 360

Define automations and chain together Data 360 processes that include ingestion (Salesforce CRM and

Amazon S3 data streams), segmentation and activation, identity resolution, and calculated insights. You

can run processes in a sequence as needed instead of waiting to run them at a scheduled time. For

example, you can chain the processes to refresh calculated insights or run segmentation when data

ingestion is completed. You can define automations to monitor flow runs or check their progress. Use

Flow Builder to create Data 360 flows. With Flow Builder, you can build complex enterprise-scale

automation with automated triggers, reusable building blocks, and prebuilt solutions.

Automate Flows in Data 360

Create a record-triggered flow to publish platform events of Data 360 actions. You can use the

published platform event to resume your paused auto-launched flow. With a record-triggered flow,

you can update another record, send a notification, initiate a process, or maintain data consistency. A

record-triggered flow runs only when a record is created or updated. It can update a record 10 times

faster than a record-change process.

Guidelines and Limits for Automations

You can configure automations based on your requirements using the Data 360 actions. When

planning an automation, make sure to review the guidelines and limits. Throttling limits the maximum

number of API requests triggered within a specified time period.

After you've combined, unified, and harmonized your data in Data 360, it's now ready for you to

personalized experience for your customers. Data 360, Tableau, and Salesforce 360 apps work

using CRM Analytics. You can build contextual insights and create interactive views on a data lake

into CRM Analytics. You can filter the Data 360 data, drill deeper, and act on the data directly from the

dashboards.

DMOs to get information on the most pertinent fields and records from Data 360. You can group,

filter, and summarize records in the report, run it for near real-time information and share it with

others. And, make business decisions faster by visualizing KPIs and trends from Data 360 reports in

Tableau enables metadata and data discovery of all objects in your Data 360 instance with Salesforce

REQUIRED EDITIONS
REQUIRED EDITIONS

Available in: Lightning Experience

The Data 360 Tableau connector provides two modes for interacting between products: live and extract.

You can select your mode in Tableau when setting up your connection by choosing the Live or Extract

radio buttons available for selection after a table has been dragged into the “Need More data?” section.

It’s suggested that you determine your desired connection and don’t change your mode after you have

begun initial execution of your queries.

Live mode is the default, but each mode and we strongly recommend using a live connection when

querying data from Tableau.

Data 360 Objects in Tableau

All Data 360 objects are accessible in Tableau by querying the authorized tenant and exposing the

objects to Tableau after authentication is complete. Data from Data 360 includes data model objects

(DMO), data lake objects (DLO), and calculated insights (CIO). All end-user modeled data is suffixed with

dlm. System-created data like calculated insights objects are suffixed with a cio. Match and merge tables

are suffixed with __dlm. Tables that include identity link in the name are exposed to Tableau.

To build Tableau visualizations from unified data, identity link files are required to be included in the

mapping in Tableau. Drag your objects from the sidebar to the Tableau canvas to map them.

1772

Data 360

Unlock Hidden Insights with Tableau

In the above image, numerous tables are being joined to visualize several data points in Data 360,

starting with the Unified Individual Table. In order to understand the Calculated Insights called purchase

insights that were defined on the unified individual, it’s mapped to the unified individual table. However,

Tableau must traverse the graph to get to a place where it can handle the relationships across all the

tables. For cases where you have a unified individual and you want to map it to an individual, you must

map the individual identity link, which is a system-created bridge table that comes from the match and

merge process and maps the individual ids to the unified individual ids. After the individual table has

been mapped, all tables that map to it can be mapped. In this case, contactpointaddress,

deviceapplication, SalesOrder__dlm, segment_membership, and websiteengagement. These are all

_dlms that can be mapped to the individual__dlm.

Finally, salesorderproduct can be mapped to SalesOrder__dlm. These joins are all loosely defined as

joins, not unions. However, Tableau doesn’t determine how the joins occur under the defined

visualization. Tableau sends a query to Data 360 to get the data in a defined fashion relative to the

mapped tables.

Note The Data 360 query engine supports consumer rights at query execution time. When

dashboards are published, ensure that any changes made to your Data 360 data as a result of

consumer rights requests, such as Right to be Forgotten or Restriction of Processing, are reflected in

Tableau.

Mapping Unified Individual Data Model Objects

Use a Tableau relationship when you define a relationship between a Unified Individual Data Model

Object (DMO) and DMOs that represent performance and interaction data from Marketing Cloud

Engagement or cases from Service Cloud. You must also map the individual identity link using Tableau

join for every engagement entity as shown in the screenshots here. It makes sure your queries fetch data

from all objects that are mapped to the Unified Individual. For more information, see Tableau

Relationships vs Joins.

Downloading Tableau Data Source File

You can download already modeled relationships for your selected data object from Data 360. You can

download the data models in the form of a Tableau data source file and import it for data exploration.

•

-
Click Data Model tab in Data 360.
-
Select one object at a time and click Download Tableau Data Source File button.
-
Download the file on your local machine as a .tds file.
-
Import the file in Tableau Desktop or Tableau Server for further data explorations.

Fully Qualified Keys in Tableau

Fully Qualified Keys (FQKs) are composite keys that are used as the primary keys in Data 360. FQKs help

resolve key conflicts that arise when data from different source systems is brought into Data 360. Keys

can conflict when data is harmonized into one data model object.

All keys include two components.

•  The primary key provided by the data source.
•  The key qualifier that’s configured within Data 360.

When you build your own data model in Tableau using data from Data 360 check if the data has key

qualifiers enabled. For adhoc table joins, you must include the key qualifier field to use a composite key.
Add  IFNULL()  function in joins if the key qualifiers aren’t configured in Data 360.

The Tableau Data Source file contains all the relationships that are defined in Data 360 data model. If key

qualifiers are enabled in your Salesforce org then they're automatically included in the relationships for
the data model. Null values in key qualifiers are also handled with  IFNULL()  function.

For more information, see Fully Qualified Keys

Data 360 and Tableau Use Cases

Tableau helps you explore, analyze, and find hidden insights in your data. The Tableau to Data Cloud

connectors use the Hyper query engine to provide fast processing. You can explore your Data 360data in

near real time enabling quick and accurate decision-making. These example use cases illustrate how

Data 360and Tableau work together to help you achieve your business goals and deliver a personalized

experience for your customers.

Auto Industry

An automobile company wants to recommend new features and services that are relevant to each

customer. The customer data is in the Marketing Cloud Engagement. The company also has other

sources for vehicle-related data (mileage, frequent locations) and personal driving data (driving patterns,

location).

In Data 360, ingest, prepare, and unify the data to create a customer record that represents a single

source of truth for each customer. Build segments to send personalized campaigns.

Create data models that you can then use to explore and analyze in Tableau.

•  Understand how your customers are using your products and services to make better and relevant

recommendations.

•  Decide on which new features would be useful and more likely to be adopted by customers in specific

regions.

•  Gather key insights that can help you make business decisions, such as problems or alerts from

vehicles based on model or driving range for electric vehicles.

Financial Services

A finance company is looking to simplify its customers’ banking experience and understand user interests

based on the various channels that a customer engages with.

To provide a customer journey that is simple and personalized, create a single and consistent view of

each customer. In Data 360, ingest data from Engagement, Sales Cloud, and other data sources, such as

banking transactions, real estate, or other financial services. Use calculated insights to determine when

and how to engage with customers. Create segments based on this information.

Visualize Your Data with Data Lens

Data Lens provides you with an intuitive and interactive environment for in-depth data exploration and

visualization. Moving beyond static reports, you can directly interact with your data to reveal hidden,

valuable insights and patterns.

With Data Lens, you can:

•  Analyze Distributions: Understand the spread of values to identify patterns and outliers.
•  Explore Relationships: Discover connections between related data points.
•  Examine Row Details: Validate summarized data by reviewing individual rows.
•  Pinpoint Nulls: Identify missing values within your datasets.
•  Categorize Unique Values: Classify data by recognizing distinct entries.
•  Understand Data Types: Determine the assigned data type for each field.
•  Streamline Your View: Hide or show fields to optimize your data perspective.

Data Lens provides these user interface features within Segments, Data Lake Objects, and Data Model

Objects tabs.

•  Profile View: Shows data columns as colored bars, summarizing data distributions, values, and nulls.

You can click values to include/exclude or highlight relationships.

•  Data Grid View: A spreadsheet-like view for viewing row-level details. Synchronized with the profile

pane for consistency.

•  List View: Show or hide fields to streamline your view.

Data Governance

Data Lens operates by leveraging the existing query layer to preview data, ensuring adherence to

established security protocols. Data Lens respects policies such as dynamic PII masking, which is applied

at the time of the query. This means only the masked version of the data is displayed in the Data Lens

preview, while the raw, unmasked data remains secure in its original location. This approach ensures

sensitive information is protected from unauthorized viewing during data exploration and preview,
aligning with strict data governance and compliance requirements.

Load Data from Data 360 into Marketing Cloud Intelligence

Connect Data 360 to Marketing Cloud Intelligence to analyze your customer data and build dashboards

and reports.

The data is refreshed daily by default. You can change the frequency schedule, but using a different

refresh rate could delay data subject rights and other compliance-based updates from flowing to

Marketing Cloud Intelligence.

You can load your data using an Intelligence Data 360 connector (TotalConnect or Granular Data Center)

or by installing the Data Cloud app from the Intelligence Marketplace.

Another connector exists in Intelligence for Data 360 (Data Cloud CI connector) and appears if you

previously used it, or if you installed the Data Cloud app. However, we recommend using the Data

360connectors instead. For more information, see Pull Data Cloud Data into Marketing Cloud

Intelligence.

Before loading data from Data 360 into Intelligence, review the prerequisites. See Prerequisites Before

Pulling Data Cloud Data.

Explore and Research Content with Notebook AI

Data 360 Notebook AI is a generative AI notebook for uploading personal, enterprise, and public

content, conducting research, and generating insights.

Notebook AI is for individual business users and teams such as sales, support, and marketing. Use it to

create a personal purpose-built workspaces for exploring content by asking questions or selecting built-in

actions.

Users create private resource libraries in the notebook, combine them with enterprise-wide content, and

produce authoritative content all in one space.

Notebook AI is for short-term, time-bound projects or long-term research and content creation, bringing

flexibility, control, and collaboration to AI-powered research.

You can use Notebook AI in Data 360 or as a web application.

Use Case: Notebook AI for Researching Repetitive Customer Support Issues

Customer support representatives often deal with repetitive customer issues that stem from underlying

product issues or configuration gaps.

Multiple systems and sources record customer issues, such as support cases, JIRA tickets, Slack threads,

and error logs related to the product. There are multiple ways to find and document solutions to the

issues, such as personal notes, product manuals, or community articles.

If there's no clear knowledge in one place that support representatives can use, reuse, or share, it can

lead to different responses and escalations. As a support engineer, use this general flow to work with

Notebook AI:

1788

Data 360

Explore and Research Content with Notebook AI

•  Create a research notebook
•  Upload all the sources into a resource library
•  Explore your sources by asking questions, reviewing responses, and validating source citations

Validate the resolution and create an authoritative article by copying or downloading your analysis. Share

and add the new content to your enterprise resource as a knowledge base article for others to benefit

from your research.

Use Case: Notebook AI for Researching a Request for Proposal (RFP)
Business Opportunity

Sales representatives can use Notebook AI to research a sales proposal for a new business opportunity.

Sales representatives can utilize an AI-Generated notebook to upload various documents into resource

libraries. These documents can include meeting notes with the customer, web pages detailing market

trends, competitor analysis reports, and the RFP.

Explore your sources by asking questions, reviewing responses, and validating source citations. Use your

research to generate a report and share it with your team for review.

Enable Notebook AI For Data Spaces and Users

Grant Data 360 Notebook AI access to data in data spaces and give enterprise users access to

Notebook AI with custom permission sets. In a multi-org architecture, enable Notebook AI in both the

home org and companion org.

Enable Notebook AI Web Access

Give enterprise users access to Data 360 Notebook AI web application. Authorize the Notebook AI

web application to connect to your Salesforce org and allow users to log in to the application from the

web.

Manage AI Notebooks

Manage your generative AI notebooks in Data 360 Notebook AI. By default, a notebook is private to

the user who creates it.

When you use Notebook AI to upload content, ask questions, and save insights, your data is processed

through Data 360 and Agentforce. Using Data 360 to process data, index content sources, and query

data has billing implications.

Create a Notebook

Use Notebook AI to explore content for research, building proposals, or analysis.

1. 1.  From App Launcher, select Data Cloud.

If you are using the Notebook AI web application, go to notebookai.salesforce.com and enter your

domain and credentials. You can also access the Notebook AI application from Salesforce orgs.

2. 2.  Select Notebook AI and click New Notebook.

3. 3.  Enter a name, select a data space, and add an appropriate description for your notebook.

You can create notebooks in the default data space and data spaces that Notebook AI has access to.

4. 4.  Click Save.

Data 360 creates a new notebook in the default workspace. Now, you can build your resource libraries

in the notebook.

Add a Resource Library and Sources

Use a resource library to group related resources. You can build or import a resource library. A notebook

can contain multiple resource libraries.

1. 1.  To add a resource library, click New Resource Library or start by adding sources to the personal library.

2. 2.  Enter a name that describes the collection of sources.

For example, you can group resource libraries for a support issue on DC Sandbox as Customer Meeting

Gemini Notes, DC Sandbox Product Doc, or DC Sandbox Community Cases.

3. 3.  To import a resource library, click Import Resource Library.

Import resource libraries from other notebooks you have access to or enterprise resources such as

search indexes created by your team.

You can also rename a resource library if your project scope changes. You can remove a resource

library if it becomes irrelevant to the scope of your research.

After you create a resource library, add sources to your library. These sources can be your personal files

like meeting notes or web links. Notebook AI supports the following file types.

Mappings to the AcademicCredential DMO Object

The Academic Credential DMO is a Data Cloud data model object (DMO) for external-facing credential

data, which typically includes information about degrees, certifications, or other academic achievements

that are issued by educational institutions.

•  The AcademicCredential DLO field  DataSource  maps to the AcademicCredential DMO Object

DataSourceId  field.

•  The AcademicCredential DLO field  DataSourceObject  maps to the AcademicCredential DMO

Object  DataSourceObjectId  field.

•  The AcademicCredential DLO field  Id  maps to the AcademicCredential DMO Object  Id  field.
•  The AcademicCredential DLO field  IssuerId  maps to the AcademicCredential DMO Object

IssuerId  field.

•  The AcademicCredential DLO field  Name  maps to the AcademicCredential DMO Object  Name  field.
•  The AcademicCredential DLO field  Type  maps to the AcademicCredential DMO Object  Type  field.

Mappings to the AcademicSession DMO Object

The Academic Session DMO is a Data Cloud data model object (DMO) for recording the course offering

period, specifying time periods based on an institution's calendar. These periods can be semesters,

quarters, trimesters, or other divisions of the academic year.

•  The AcademicSession DLO field  AcademicTermId  maps to the AcademicSession DMO Object

AcademicTermId  field.

•  The AcademicSession DLO field  AddDropDeadline  maps to the AcademicSession DMO Object

AddDropDeadlineDateTime  field.

•  The AcademicSession DLO field  AuditDueDate  maps to the AcademicSession DMO Object

AuditDueDateTime  field.

•  The AcademicSession DLO field  ClassEndDate  maps to the AcademicSession DMO Object

ClassEndDateTime  field.
